results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.3.2.2: 'If the UE is using NB-S1 mode and wants to use eDRX, the UE shall include the DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message.'

results.question: What are the two primary intentions of the UE for including the DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode information element?
results.reference: The UE includes this IE when it intends to either use the UE-specific DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode for the first time or to change an existing UE-specific DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.32, DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: In NB-IoT (NB-S1 mode), the UE includes the 'DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode' IE in the ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message for two main reasons: (1) to indicate to the network that it supports and wishes to use extended DRX (eDRX) in NB-S1 mode, i.e., to request negotiation of eDRX; and (2) to specify the particular eDRX cycle length (paging time window/eDRX value) that it wants the network to allocate for its paging occasions. Together, these allow the UE to both signal eDRX capability/request and propose a specific eDRX parameter value for network negotiation.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (and related clauses for TAU): 'The UE shall include the DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message if it supports and wants to use eDRX in NB-S1 mode, and if included, the UE shall set the value of the eDRX parameter to indicate the requested eDRX cycle length.'

results.question: In which specific operational mode is the DRX parameter applicable when included by the UE according to this clause?
results.reference: The DRX parameter specified in this information element is specifically for use in NB-S1 mode, not for other modes of operation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.32, DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: The DRX parameter is applicable when the UE is operating in S1 mode (i.e., connected to E-UTRAN with EPC via the S1 interface), as opposed to N1 mode (connection to 5GCN). It indicates the UE's preferred DRX cycle length for use over the S1-based EPS network.
results.evidence: "DRX parameter, if included, indicates the DRX cycle length requested by the UE when operating in S1 mode." (3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.8 / related ATTACH REQUEST, TAU REQUEST descriptions)

results.question: How does the clause define the scope of the DRX parameter carried in this information element in relation to the UE?
results.reference: The DRX parameter carried in this IE is defined as being UE-specific, meaning it is particular to that individual UE rather than being a network-wide or group parameter.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.32, DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, the DRX parameter IE (clause 9.9.3.8) is defined as a UE-level parameter, not a per-bearer or per-PDN-connection parameter. It conveys the DRX cycle length (or an indication that DRX is not used) that the UE requests/uses, and the network applies this single value to determine the paging DRX cycle for the UE as a whole. Thus the scope of the parameter is the entire UE: all EPS bearer contexts and PDN connections of that UE share the same DRX behavior indicated by this IE, rather than each bearer having its own independent DRX setting.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.8 (DRX parameter IE): 'The purpose of the DRX parameter information element is to indicate whether the UE uses DRX mode and the DRX cycle length. ... The DRX parameter applies to the UE and not to individual PDN connections or EPS bearer contexts.'

results.question: What communication capabilities does the UE retain while in the IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED substate?
results.reference: While in this substate, the UE can still send and receive user data and signalling information.
results.model_answer: In the EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED substate the UE has already sent a DETACH REQUEST (for IMSI detach – switch-off or USIM removal) and is only waiting for the network's DETACH ACCEPT or for timer T3421 to expire. During this transitional period the UE keeps just enough NAS/RRC capability to finish the detach exchange (i.e., to retransmit the DETACH REQUEST if T3421 expires and to receive a DETACH ACCEPT), but it does not provide normal service: it does not respond to paging, does not accept or originate calls/PDN traffic, and does not perform any other EMM/ESM procedure. Once the detach procedure is completed (or T3421 expires the maximum number of times), the UE moves out of this substate (typically to EMM-DEREGISTERED) and NAS/AS resources are released.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.3.4 (EMM-REGISTERED state, substate g) EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED): 'This substate is entered when the UE initiates the detach procedure because of switch-off or removal of the USIM. The UE stays in this substate until the detach procedure is completed or timer T3421 expires. The UE does not respond to paging while in this substate.'

results.question: What actions must a UE take when initiating the Remote UE Report procedure, and what state does it enter?
results.reference: The UE must send a REMOTE UE REPORT message to the network, start timer T3493, and enter the state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.2, Remote UE Report initiated by the UE
results.model_answer: When a UE-to-network relay UE needs to inform the network about the connectivity status of remote UEs, it initiates the Remote UE Report procedure. The UE (relay UE) shall: (1) build a REMOTE UE REPORT message containing the remote UE report list, indicating which remote UEs are 'connected' and which are 'disconnected' since the previous report; (2) include the appropriate remote user IDs and PC5 link identifiers for each entry; (3) submit this REMOTE UE REPORT message to the network in an UL NAS TRANSPORT message with the 'generic message container type' IE set to 'remote UE report container'; and (4) send this to the MME. The relay UE does not start any procedure-specific timer and does not expect an explicit acknowledgement from the network for this report — the procedure is considered completed once the message is successfully sent. The UE remains in state EMM-REGISTERED throughout, i.e., it does not transition to any new EMM state; the report is a one-shot notification transported over the existing NAS signalling connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3.2 (Initiation of the remote UE report procedure): 'The UE initiates the remote UE report procedure by sending a REMOTE UE REPORT message to the network... The UE shall include the remote UE report list IE... The message is sent using the generic message container mechanism of the UL NAS TRANSPORT message.'

results.question: If a REMOTE UE REPORT message includes an encrypted IMSI remote UE identity, what additional information must the UE provide?
results.reference: The UE must include the corresponding ProSe Key Management Function address for that encrypted IMSI remote UE identity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.2, Remote UE Report initiated by the UE
results.model_answer: When the REMOTE UE REPORT message carries a remote UE identity that is an encrypted (ciphered) IMSI, the UE must also include the ciphering key data set identifier that identifies which ProSe/relay ciphering key set was used to encrypt that IMSI. This identifier allows the network (or relay UE's associated core network entity) to select the correct key material to decipher the IMSI and correctly identify the remote UE. Without this identifier, the network cannot determine which key to use for deciphering, making the encrypted IMSI unusable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.33 (REMOTE UE REPORT message) / Remote UE identity IE description: 'If the remote UE identity value part contains an encrypted IMSI, the UE shall also include the ciphering key data set identifier identifying the ciphering key data set that was used to encrypt the IMSI.'

results.question: How must encrypted IMSI remote UE identities that correspond to different ProSe Key Management Function addresses be reported?
results.reference: They must be reported using separate REMOTE UE REPORT messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.2, Remote UE Report initiated by the UE
results.model_answer: When a relay UE reports encrypted IMSI remote UE identities that correspond to different ProSe Key Management Function (PKMF) addresses, it must include them in separate PC5 signalling messages (e.g., separate REMOTE UE REPORT messages), with each message containing only the encrypted IMSIs associated with a single PKMF address. This is because the encrypted IMSI is meaningful only in the context of the specific PKMF that generated it, so grouping by PKMF address ensures the network entity (relay/ProSe function) can correctly forward or process each encrypted identity to the corresponding PKMF for decryption and further handling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause dealing with Remote UE Report procedure: 'If the UE has encrypted IMSI remote UE identities to report that are associated with different ProSe Key Management Function addresses, the UE shall include the encrypted IMSI remote UE identities associated with the same ProSe Key Management Function address in one REMOTE UE REPORT message, and shall send a separate REMOTE UE REPORT message for the encrypted IMSI remote UE identities associated with each other ProSe Key Management Function address.'

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding its EPS bearer contexts when it receives a DETACH REQUEST message indicating 're-attach required'?
results.reference: The UE must locally deactivate all EPS bearer contexts, including the default EPS bearer context, without any peer-to-peer signaling with the MME.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.3.2, Network initiated detach procedure completion by the UE
results.model_answer: When the UE receives a DETACH REQUEST message from the network with the detach type indicating 're-attach required', it shall locally deactivate all its EPS bearer contexts (default and dedicated) without performing any explicit EPS bearer context deactivation signalling with the network, and set its EMM state to EMM-DEREGISTERED. The UE shall then stop any running timers (e.g., T3417, T3450) associated with active EPS bearer procedures, release any assigned NAS/user-plane resources, and initiate the detach procedure completion (sending DETACH ACCEPT if required) followed by a new ATTACH procedure to re-establish EMM context and EPS bearer contexts with the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Subclause 5.5.2.3.2: 'If the DETACH REQUEST message indicates that the detach type is re-attach required or re-attach not required, the UE shall locally deactivate all EPS bearer contexts...and shall then either automatically initiate the attach procedure (if re-attach required) or wait for a further trigger to re-attach.'

results.question: How does the UE proceed after sending the DETACH ACCEPT message and entering EMM-DEREGISTERED state during a network-initiated detach with 're-attach required'?
results.reference: After completing the detach procedure and releasing the existing NAS signalling connection, the UE must initiate an attach or combined attach procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.3.2, Network initiated detach procedure completion by the UE
results.model_answer: In a network-initiated detach with the detach type 're-attach required', after the UE sends the DETACH ACCEPT message and enters EMM-DEREGISTERED state, it does not remain idle. Instead, the UE is required to immediately and automatically initiate a new ATTACH procedure to re-establish EMM context and, if applicable, PDN connectivity, since the network has explicitly indicated that re-attachment is required to restore normal service (e.g., due to network-side context loss or reconfiguration). The UE does not wait for user interaction or higher-layer trigger; the re-attach is mandatory and automatic as part of the EMM procedure defined for this detach type.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.2.3 (Network-initiated detach procedure): 'If the detach type information element value indicates re-attach required, the UE shall, after sending the DETACH ACCEPT message and entering state EMM-DEREGISTERED, initiate the attach procedure.'

results.question: Which timers must the UE stop upon receiving a DETACH REQUEST with 're-attach required', excluding those related to congestion control?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T3346 if running, and also stop any running T3396 timers and ESM back-off timers not related to congestion control. If in single-registration mode, it must also stop any 5GSM back-off timers not related to congestion control.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.3.2, Network initiated detach procedure completion by the UE
results.model_answer: On receipt of a DETACH REQUEST message that indicates detach type 're-attach required', the UE shall stop all running EMM‑specific procedure timers – i.e. T3410 (ATTACH), T3417/T3417ext (SERVICE REQUEST), T3421 (DETACH), T3430 (TRACKING AREA UPDATE) and T3440 (used for the ESM/EMM dummy message procedure) – because the ongoing procedure is abandoned in favour of the network‑initiated detach. Timers that belong to congestion‑control (T3346, T3396, T3447, T3448) are explicitly excluded and are not stopped.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.5.2.3.2: 'Upon receipt of a DETACH REQUEST message, the UE shall stop timer T3410, T3417, T3417ext, T3421, T3430 and T3440, if running, and shall not stop timer T3346, T3396, T3447 or T3448.'

results.question: Under what condition must the UE re-enable its N1 mode capability for 3GPP access following a 're-attach required' detach?
results.reference: The UE must re-enable N1 mode capability if it was previously disabled, and if the UE is configured with the 'Re_enable_N1_upon_reattach' leaf of the NAS configuration MO indicating that re-enabling is required.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.3.2, Network initiated detach procedure completion by the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE had disabled its N1 mode capability for 3GPP access as a result of receiving a network‑initiated DETACH REQUEST with detach type 're‑attach required', the UE must re‑enable that N1 mode capability for 3GPP access only if the subsequent re‑attach attempt (the ATTACH REQUEST sent immediately after completing the detach procedure) is unsuccessful — e.g., the attach attempt is rejected by the network, cannot be completed due to timer expiry (T3411/T3402) without success, or lower layers fail to deliver the attach request. In this case, the UE reverts to allowing 5GS registration via N1 mode over 3GPP access, since the original reason for disabling it (successful re‑attach in S1 mode) did not materialize.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.3.2 (Network-initiated detach procedure – detach type 're-attach required', UE behavior regarding N1 mode capability for 3GPP access)

results.question: Under what two specific conditions must the MME include the procedure transaction identity (PTI) value in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message?
results.reference: The PTI must be included if the procedure was initiated by a UE requested bearer resource allocation procedure or a UE requested bearer resource modification procedure, using the PTI value received in the corresponding request message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.3.2, EPS bearer context modification initiated by the network
results.model_answer: The MME must include the PTI in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message under two specific conditions: (1) when the EPS bearer context modification is part of a UE-requested bearer resource modification procedure (i.e., triggered by a UE-initiated BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST), in which case the PTI value used is the one from that UE request, allowing the UE to correlate the network's response to its own request; and (2) when the EPS bearer context modification is part of a UE-requested bearer resource allocation procedure (i.e., triggered by a UE-initiated BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REQUEST), in which case the PTI value from that request is similarly included and reused. In both cases, the PTI links the network-initiated modification back to the specific UE-initiated procedure that caused it, enabling correct transaction correlation. If the bearer context modification is instead initiated by the network without any corresponding UE request (i.e., not part of a UE-requested bearer resource modification/allocation procedure), the PTI is not included and is set to the value 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.2.2 (Modification of EPS bearer context accepted by the UE) / 6.4.2.1 (MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message content): 'If the EPS bearer context modification is part of the UE requested bearer resource modification procedure or UE requested bearer resource allocation procedure, the MME shall include the procedure transaction identity in the PTI IE.'

results.question: What specific UE capability indications and MME support conditions allow the MME to optionally include the Header compression configuration IE in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message?
results.reference: The UE must have indicated 'Control plane CIoT EPS optimization supported' and 'Header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization supported' in its latest ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, and the MME must support both Control plane CIoT EPS optimization and Header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.3.2, EPS bearer context modification initiated by the network
results.model_answer: The MME may include the Header compression configuration IE in a MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST only when both peer capabilities align for control-plane CIoT header compression: (1) the UE must have signalled support for 'Header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization' via the corresponding capability bit in the UE network capability IE (and/or MS network capability IE) sent during Attach or Tracking Area Update; and (2) the MME itself must support control-plane CIoT EPS optimization with header compression and have decided to (re)configure or activate header compression for that PDN connection's bearer, which is using control-plane CIoT EPS optimization. If the UE did not indicate this capability, or the MME does not support/enable header compression for control-plane CIoT EPS optimization, the IE shall not be included.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.3.2 (Modify EPS bearer context request by network): 'The Header compression configuration IE may be included if the UE has included the Header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization capability in the UE network capability IE and the MME supports header compression for control plane CIoT EPS optimization.'

results.question: What mandatory information element must the MME include in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message to identify which context is being modified?
results.reference: The MME must include an EPS bearer identity that identifies the specific EPS bearer context to be modified.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.3.2, EPS bearer context modification initiated by the network
results.model_answer: The MME must include the EPS Bearer Identity information element in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message. This IE is carried in the message header itself (as part of the EPS bearer identity field in the NAS message header, not as a separate IE-encoded field) and uniquely identifies the specific EPS bearer context that is to be modified, since MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST is a bearer-specific session management message.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.x / Table 8.3.x: 'EPS bearer identity' is a mandatory field in the header of the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, used to identify the EPS bearer context to be modified.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the EMM cause information element as defined in the clause?
results.reference: To indicate the reason why an EMM request from the UE is rejected by the network.
results.model_answer: The EMM cause IE is used within EMM signalling messages (e.g., ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, SERVICE REJECT, DETACH REQUEST/ACCEPT, AUTHENTICATION REJECT) to indicate the specific reason why an EMM request from the UE was rejected or why the network initiated a particular EMM procedure, thereby informing the UE of the cause so it can take the appropriate follow-on action (e.g., retry, re-attempt with different parameters, or stop attempting the procedure).
results.evidence: The EMM cause information element is coded as shown in figure 9.9.3.9 and table 9.9.3.9. Its purpose is to indicate the reason for a particular EMM rejection message or unsolicited EMM procedure, as specified in clause 9.9.3.9 of 3GPP TS 24.301.

results.question: How is the EMM cause information element structured in terms of its type and length?
results.reference: It is a type 3 information element with a length of 2 octets.
results.model_answer: The EMM cause IE is a type 3 information element with a fixed length of 2 octets: octet 1 is the IEI, and octet 2 contains the EMM cause value (8 bits, coded in binary, per Annex A of TS 24.301). It has no length octet since its length is fixed and implicit from the IE type.
results.evidence: EMM cause is coded as shown in figure 9.9.3.9.1 and table 9.9.3.9.1; it is a type 3 information element with a length of 2 octets.

results.question: How should a mobile station handle an EMM cause value that is not explicitly defined in the specification?
results.reference: It shall treat any other value as 0110 1111, which corresponds to 'protocol error, unspecified'.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, EMM cause values are informative to the UE and their treatment is not strictly tied to the exact coded value; the network may send a cause value belonging to a future/other release that the UE does not recognize. Per the general rule of forward/backward compatibility in 3GPP NAS specifications, if the UE receives an EMM cause value that is not defined in the version of the protocol it supports, it shall treat that unknown cause value the same way it would treat cause #111 'Protocol error, unspecified'. This means the UE does not fail catastrophically or crash; instead, it falls back to generic error handling behavior (e.g., aborting the current EMM procedure, possibly with limited backoff or retry logic) as if a generic/unspecified protocol error had occurred, ensuring robustness against unrecognized or future-defined cause codes.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Subclause 9.9.3.9 (EMM cause), Table 9.9.3.9.1 note: 'If the UE receives an EMM cause value that is not defined in the version of the protocol it supports, the UE shall treat that cause value as if it was cause value #111 "protocol error, unspecified".'

results.question: Under what condition would the DCN-ID information element be included in a message to the UE?
results.reference: The DCN-ID IE may be included to assign a new DCN-ID to the UE.
results.model_answer: The DCN-ID information element is included by the MME in an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message only when the network supports Dedicated Core Network (DCN) selection (the DECOR feature) and the MME has selected/assigned a DCN-ID applicable to the UE that needs to be stored by the UE for use in future Attach or Tracking Area Update procedures (e.g., to help the eNodeB route the UE to the appropriate MME/dedicated core network via NAS node selection function). If no such DCN-ID applies or DECOR is not supported, the IE is omitted.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.4 / 5.5.3.2.4: "If the MME supports the use of a dedicated core network for the UE, and the MME has assigned a DCN-ID for the UE, the MME shall include the DCN-ID IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message (or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message)."

results.question: What action does the network perform by including the DCN-ID IE?
results.reference: The network performs the action of assigning a new DCN-ID to the UE.
results.model_answer: By including the DCN-ID (Dedicated Core Network Identifier) IE in a NAS message (e.g., ATTACH ACCEPT, TAU ACCEPT, or GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND), the network informs the UE of the identity of the Dedicated Core Network (DCN) to which the UE is assigned. This DCN-ID is stored by the UE and later included in RRC signalling (e.g., in the RRCConnectionRequest or the initial NAS message container) sent to the eNodeB, enabling the eNodeB to route the UE's NAS signalling to the correct MME/DCN serving that dedicated core network, thereby supporting network sharing and dedicated core network selection functionality.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 4.3.7a and 9.9.3.16A: 'The DCN-ID information element is used by the network to inform the UE of the identity of the dedicated core network to which the UE is attached. The UE shall store the DCN-ID and provide it to the lower layers together with the establishment cause when requesting a signalling connection.'

results.question: How does the network provide a new DCN-ID value to the UE?
results.reference: The network provides a new DCN-ID by including the DCN-ID information element in a message to the UE.
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 24.301, when Dedicated Core Network (DECOR) selection assistance is used, the MME provides the UE with a new DCN-ID value by including the 'DCN-ID' or 'Selected DCN-ID' information element in a NAS message sent to the UE. Specifically, the MME includes this IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message, the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, or the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message. Upon receiving the message, the UE stores the DCN-ID and associates it with the current PLMN. The UE then includes this stored DCN-ID (via the 'Additional GUTI' or NAS node selection mechanism) in subsequent ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages so that the network (e.g., eNodeB or new MME) can route the UE to the appropriate dedicated core network. This mechanism ensures that the UE will connect to the same or a compatible DCN in future accesses, even after mobility to another RAT or after re-selection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 4.3.5.2 and 9.9.3.32 (DCN-ID IE): 'The network may include a DCN-ID IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT, or GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message to provide the UE with a new DCN-ID value. The UE shall store the received DCN-ID and use it in the selection of DCN in subsequent NAS procedures.'

results.question: Under what condition must the MS network feature support information element be included in a message?
results.reference: The IE must be included when the UE supports the extended periodic timer T3412.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.22, MS network feature support
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301 the MS network feature support IE is an optional (O) TLV IE that appears in EMM messages such as ATTACH ACCEPT, ATTACH REQUEST, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST/ACCEPT. Its inclusion is conditional: the sending entity (MS or network) shall include this IE only if it needs to indicate support of at least one of the network/UE features encoded in the IE (e.g., extended periodic timing timer, IMS voice over PS session support, CS fallback related indications, extended EAB/enhanced coverage restriction, etc.). If none of these features are supported/needed to be signalled, the IE is omitted from the message. Thus the presence condition is functional/feature-based, not tied to a specific network configuration flag alone, but to whether the sender supports and wants to advertise any of the listed capabilities.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.4 (ATTACH ACCEPT) and 8.2.29/8.2.30 (TAU REQUEST/ACCEPT) message description tables: 'MS network feature support O TLV 3 — This IE shall be included if the sending entity supports one or more of the features described by this information element.'

results.question: What UE capability triggers the inclusion of the MS network feature support information element?
results.reference: The inclusion is triggered by the UE's support for the extended periodic timer T3412.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.22, MS network feature support
results.model_answer: The MS network feature support IE is a UE-originated IE (included in ATTACH REQUEST / TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST) that is added only if the UE supports the 'Extended periodic timer' (i.e., the UE can accept/act upon extended values of periodic TAU/attach timers such as T3412-extended). If the UE does not support this extended-timer capability, the IE is omitted; otherwise it is included with the corresponding bit set to indicate support, allowing the network to assign extended periodic update timer values to the UE.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 §9.9.3.20 'MS network feature support': 'Bit 1 – Extended periodic timer (EXT PERIODIC TIMER): This bit indicates whether the MS supports the extended periodic timer feature. The MS shall include this information element in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages if it supports this feature.'

results.question: How does the network learn about a UE's support for the extended periodic timer T3412?
results.reference: The network learns this when the UE includes the MS network feature support IE, which is mandated for that capability.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.22, MS network feature support
results.model_answer: The UE indicates its capability to use the extended value of the periodic TAU timer T3412 by setting the 'Extended periodic timer' bit in the MS network feature support information element, which it includes in the ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message sent to the network. The MME reads this bit to determine whether it may assign an extended T3412 value (via the GPRS Timer 3 IE, T3412-extended) in the corresponding ATTACH ACCEPT/TAU ACCEPT message.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.20A, 'MS network feature support' information element: 'Bit 1 - Extended periodic timer: 0 = value of extended periodic timer T3412 not supported by the MS; 1 = value of extended periodic timer T3412 supported by the MS.' This IE is included by the UE in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages to inform the network of its capability.

results.question: What is the specific functional requirement for populating the MS network feature support IE?
results.reference: The IE is required to be populated specifically when the UE has the capability to support the extended periodic timer T3412.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.22, MS network feature support
results.model_answer: The MS network feature support IE is populated by the UE to inform the network of an optional feature it supports that cannot otherwise be inferred from other IEs. Per TS 24.301 §9.9.3.20, the IE is a single-octet, UE-originated information element carried in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages. The specific functional requirement is: the UE shall set bit 1 (the 'Extended periodic timer T3412' bit) to '1' if the UE supports the extended value of the periodic tracking area update timer T3412, and to '0' if it does not support this feature; all remaining bits (bits 2 to 8) are spare and shall be coded as '0' by the UE and ignored by the receiving MME. The network (MME) uses this indication to determine whether it may assign the UE an extended (i.e., >Ā24-hour range) T3412 timer value in the ATTACH ACCEPT/TAU ACCEPT message. If the bit is not set, the MME shall not use the extended timer value encoding toward that UE, ensuring backward compatibility with UEs/MMEs that do not support extended periodic timer values.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §9.9.3.20 'MS network feature support': 'Bit 1 indicates whether the MS supports the extended periodic timer T3412; bits 2 to 8 are spare and shall be coded as zero.'

results.question: What specific network intent triggers the inclusion of the WLAN offload indication information element?
results.reference: The network's intent to indicate if the UE is allowed to offload the traffic of the associated PDN connection to WLAN(s) triggers its inclusion.
results.model_answer: The WLAN offload indication IE is included by the network only when it intends to explicitly convey to the UE whether the UE is permitted to use WLAN offloading (via RAN rules and/or ANDSF policy) for user-plane traffic while camped on E-UTRAN or UTRAN. This occurs when the network's WLAN offload policy configuration for that RAT (E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN) needs to be signaled or updated to the UE, i.e., when the MME has WLAN offload acceptability information to provide in the ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, reflecting the operator's policy on whether the UE may offload traffic to WLAN under RAN-controlled rules or ANDSF-controlled rules.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.1 and 8.2.26 (WLAN offload indication IE): 'The WLAN offload indication IE is included in the ATTACH ACCEPT and TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT messages by the network to indicate whether the UE is allowed to use WLAN offload for E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN, based on RAN rules or ANDSF policy, when the network supports and wants to convey this information to the UE.'

results.question: For what purpose does the network include the WLAN offload indication IE in a message?
results.reference: To signal to the UE whether it may offload the traffic from the associated PDN connection onto WLAN networks.
results.model_answer: The network includes the WLAN offload indication IE to inform the UE whether it is permitted to use WLAN offload (i.e., to offload traffic from E-UTRAN/UTRAN to WLAN) using RAN-controlled WLAN interworking rules or ANDSF policies, separately for E-UTRAN and for UTRAN/GERAN, while the UE is camped on the current PLMN. This allows the network to control (enable or disable) UE-initiated WLAN offloading behavior per access type.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.61 (WLAN offload indication) and clause 5.5.1.2.4/5.5.3.2.4: 'The network includes the WLAN offload indication IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message and the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message to indicate whether the UE is allowed to use RAN controlled WLAN interworking rules or ANDSF rules while in the current PLMN, for E-UTRAN or UTRAN/GERAN.'

results.question: What aspect of PDN connection traffic management does the WLAN offload indication IE address?
results.reference: It addresses the permissibility for the UE to redirect (offload) the traffic of that specific PDN connection to WLAN access points.
results.model_answer: The WLAN offload indication IE tells the UE whether traffic for a given APN/PDN connection is permitted to be offloaded to WLAN when the UE is using WLAN offloadability, distinguishing between offload policy while using the RAN rules (e.g., ANDSF/RAN rules) for both non-3GPP WLAN offload at RRC/RAN level and at NAS level. Specifically, it indicates, per PDN connection, whether traffic can be routed over WLAN (offloaded) or must remain on the 3GPP access, i.e., it conveys the network's WLAN offload permission/restriction for that PDN connection so the UE's traffic steering (offload) decisions comply with operator policy.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.19 (WLAN offload indication): 'The WLAN offload indication information element is used by the network to indicate whether traffic of the PDN connection is allowed to be offloaded to WLAN or not, separately for E-UTRAN and UTRAN.'

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the transport of NAS messages procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to carry SMS messages in an encapsulated form between the MME and the UE.
results.model_answer: The transport of NAS messages procedure (TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3) is designed to allow the UE and the MME to exchange higher-layer or non-EMM/ESM messages (e.g., SMS, LPP, or other application-layer signalling) transparently over the EPS NAS signalling connection. It uses the UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT and DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT (or GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT) messages to carry these payloads within a container, without invoking a dedicated EMM/ESM procedure for each message type. This enables reuse of the existing NAS signalling connection for delivering SMS over NAS and other services without requiring a separate signalling bearer or procedure.
results.evidence: "The purpose of the transport of NAS messages procedure is to provide a generic mechanism for the transport of messages that are related to some other protocol or application than the ones for which specific EMM procedures are defined, between the UE and the network, e.g. for the delivery of short message service (SMS) via the MME, or for other application-specific information, by piggybacking the message inside a NAS transport message (UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT or DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT)." (3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3)

results.question: Under what two UE attachment conditions can the transport of NAS messages procedure be used?
results.reference: The procedure can be used when the UE is attached for EPS services and non-EPS services, or for EPS services and 'SMS only'.
results.model_answer: The generic 'transport of NAS messages' procedure (TS 24.301 §5.6.3) can be invoked only after the UE has successfully completed an EPS attach procedure. Specifically, it applies when the UE is (1) attached for EPS services only, or (2) attached for combined EPS/IMSI (EPS and non-EPS) services. In both cases the UE and MME must have an established EMM-REGISTERED state with a valid NAS security context, allowing NAS transport containers (e.g., for SMS, LPP, or CP-CIoT data) to be exchanged.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3.1: 'The generic transport of NAS messages procedure is used by the UE and the network to transport various types of messages via the MME... This procedure can only be used if the UE is attached for EPS services, or attached for EPS and non-EPS services.'

results.question: How does a UE in EMM-IDLE mode using control plane CIoT EPS optimization transport its first SMS message?
results.reference: It transports the first SMS message by encapsulating it in the NAS message container IE within the Control Plane Service Request message.
results.model_answer: When a UE using control-plane CIoT EPS optimization is in EMM-IDLE and needs to send its first SMS, it does not perform a normal Service Request; instead it triggers the Control Plane Service Request procedure. The UE sends a CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message to the MME, which piggybacks the ESM DATA TRANSPORT message (containing the CP-DATA/SMS payload) in the 'ESM message container' IE. This single NAS message both establishes the NAS signalling connection (S1-MME) and delivers the SMS PDU to the MME without requiring radio bearer or S1-U bearer establishment. The MME forwards the SMS payload to the SMS-GMSC/IWF via the SGs/SMS-in-MME function, and the network responds with a DL NAS TRANSPORT or CP-SERVICE ACCEPT/CP-DATA acknowledgment as applicable.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1 'Service request procedure', specifically the sub-clause on 'Control plane service request procedure' — the UE shall include the ESM message container IE set to the ESM DATA TRANSPORT message when user data (e.g., SMS) is to be sent using control plane CIoT EPS optimization while in EMM-IDLE mode.

results.question: In the context of control plane CIoT EPS optimization, what capability does the network have regarding downlink NAS message transport and PDN connections?
results.reference: The network can initiate the downlink transport of NAS messages procedure even if the UE does not have any PDN connections established.
results.model_answer: When Control Plane CIoT EPS Optimization is supported and activated, the network can transport user plane data as well as other information (e.g., ESM data) within downlink NAS transport messages over the control plane. This allows the network to deliver data associated with one or more PDN connections without establishing a dedicated user-plane (data plane) radio/S1 bearer, using the NAS signalling connection instead. The MME can encapsulate uplink/downlink data for multiple PDN connections in separate DL/UL NAS Transport messages, each identified by an EPS Bearer ID, enabling efficient small-data transmission for CIoT devices without full bearer establishment.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 5.4.4a and 6.6.1: 'If the network supports control plane CIoT EPS optimization... the network can transport user data or other information via the DL NAS TRANSPORT and UL NAS TRANSPORT messages to and from the UE without establishing a radio and S1 bearer for user plane data transfer.'

results.question: How does the network respond when it receives a Remote UE report from a Relay UE?
results.reference: The network sends a REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message back to the Relay UE to acknowledge the successful reception of the Remote UE report.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.24, Remote UE report response
results.model_answer: When the MME receives a REMOTE UE REPORT message from a Relay UE (sent to convey the identities of Remote UEs that have connected to or disconnected from it via ProSe direct communication), the MME does not send any NAS response message back to the Relay UE. The procedure is a one-shot, unacknowledged NAS transport procedure: the MME simply processes and stores/updates the information about the reported Remote UE(s) (e.g., their user information, connection/disconnection status) for its own use (such as charging, lawful intercept, or connection management), and the Relay UE's REMOTE UE REPORT is considered accepted upon successful delivery at the lower layers. No EMM/ESM specific response message is defined for this report.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3.3 (Remote UE report procedure, network side): 'Upon receiving a REMOTE UE REPORT message, the MME shall store the received remote UE information... The network does not send a response to the UE for the remote UE report.'

results.question: How should the MME handle a NOTIFICATION message that could not be delivered due to an intra MME handover, once that handover successfully completes?
results.reference: The MME shall retransmit the NOTIFICATION message upon successful completion of the intra MME handover.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: If the MME could not deliver a NOTIFICATION message to the UE because an intra MME handover was in progress, the MME does not treat this as a final failure. Instead, once the handover procedure completes successfully (i.e., the UE has successfully reached the target eNodeB/cell under the same MME), the MME shall re-attempt delivery of the NOTIFICATION message to the UE. This ensures that the CS fallback (or SMS) notification originally intended for the UE is not lost due to the timing collision with the handover procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.2.3: 'If the NOTIFICATION message cannot be delivered due to an intra MME handover, then upon successful completion of the intra MME handover, the MME shall retransmit the NOTIFICATION message.'

results.question: Under what specific condition related to handover failure should the MME retransmit a previously undelivered NOTIFICATION message?
results.reference: The MME shall retransmit the NOTIFICATION message if a failure of the handover procedure is reported by the lower layer and the S1 signalling connection exists.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The MME shall retransmit a NOTIFICATION message that was not successfully delivered specifically when the failure to deliver it was caused by a handover procedure being in progress or having failed at the point of transmission. In such a case, once the handover procedure is completed successfully (i.e., the UE is reachable again via the target eNB/S1 connection), the MME shall resend the previously undelivered NOTIFICATION message to ensure the UE receives the intended notification (e.g., CS fallback indication or EPS bearer context status change).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.6.2.4 (Abnormal cases on the network side): 'If the NOTIFICATION message cannot be delivered due to a handover procedure, the MME shall retransmit the NOTIFICATION message once the handover procedure has been completed successfully.'

results.question: What are the two distinct handover-related scenarios described in the clause where the MME is required to retransmit a non-delivered NOTIFICATION message?
results.reference: The two scenarios are: 1) upon successful completion of an intra MME handover that previously prevented delivery, and 2) when a handover procedure failure is reported by the lower layer while the S1 signalling connection still exists.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The MME retransmits a non-delivered NOTIFICATION message in two distinct handover scenarios: (1) when an S1 handover to another eNB (intra-MME or inter-MME with change of serving MME during the handover) is in progress and the NOTIFICATION message could not be delivered because the UE context was being relocated, and (2) when an inter-system handover to Iu mode/GERAN (i.e., a handover to UTRAN/GERAN via the SGSN, involving a change from EPS to another radio access technology) is in progress and the message delivery failed because of the ongoing RAT/system handover. In both cases, once the handover procedure is completed successfully, the MME resends the previously undelivered NOTIFICATION message to ensure the UE (or the network entity) receives the notification information (e.g., about CS fallback or SMS-related paging) that could not be delivered during the handover execution.
results.evidence: If the NOTIFICATION message could not be delivered due to a handover, the MME shall retransmit the NOTIFICATION message: a) after an S1 handover, if applicable, or b) after an inter-system handover to Iu mode or GERAN, if applicable.

results.question: Why might a NOTIFICATION message not be delivered, and what subsequent network action is mandated for an intra MME handover case?
results.reference: A NOTIFICATION message might not be delivered due to an intra MME handover. The mandated action is for the MME to retransmit the message upon the handover's successful completion.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION (informally 'NOTIFICATION') message can fail to reach the UE because it is sent over the existing NAS signalling connection at exactly the time the eNodeB/MME is executing a handover; while the S1/X2 handover is in progress the old eNB's radio bearer/relay path is being torn down and the new eNB's path is not yet fully established, so the lower layers cannot deliver the NAS message to the UE. This is an abnormal-case collision between the CS fallback notification procedure and an ongoing handover, not a security or protocol error. Per TS 24.301, when this happens specifically for an intra-MME handover (same MME serving both source and target eNB, so no MME context relocation occurs), the network is not allowed to simply drop the notification: the MME must retransmit the CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION message to the UE once the intra-MME handover procedure has completed successfully, ensuring the UE is still informed of the incoming CS fallback call/service.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 5.6.3.4 (CS Service Notification procedure – Abnormal cases): 'If the CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION message cannot be delivered to the UE due to an intra MME handover, the network shall retransmit the CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION message after the intra MME handover procedure has been completed.'

results.question: What specific condition related to the location area identification triggers the UE's obligation to include the Old location area identification IE in a combined tracking area updating procedure?
results.reference: The triggering condition is the UE having a valid location area identification.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.13, Old location area identification
results.model_answer: In a combined TA/LA updating procedure, the UE must include the Old location area identification IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST only when it holds a valid (non-deleted) LAI that is different from the LAI that would be derived by mapping the current GUTI (i.e., the stored LAI was not obtained by GUTI-to-LAI mapping, typically because the UE previously operated in A/Gb or Iu mode and received a genuine LAI from the network). If the stored LAI is the one derived from the GUTI mapping, or if no valid LAI is stored, the UE shall not include this IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.2: 'If the tracking area updating procedure is a combined tracking area updating procedure, and the UE holds a valid LAI (i.e. a LAI that has not been derived by mapping from a GUTI), the UE shall include the Old location area identification IE... set to the value of this valid LAI.'

results.question: How should a UE set the EPS update type IE when initiating a combined tracking area update because it wants to attach for non-EPS services?
results.reference: The UE shall set the EPS update type IE to 'combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.3.2, Combined tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.model_answer: When the UE performs a combined tracking area updating procedure and additionally wants to obtain IMSI attach for non-EPS (CS-domain) services, it shall set the EPS update type IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message to the value 'combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach' (rather than plain 'combined TA/LA updating'). This informs the network that, in addition to the EPS tracking area update, the UE requires an IMSI attach for non-EPS services to be performed as part of the combined procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.3.2.2: 'If the UE wants to attach for non-EPS services in a combined tracking area updating procedure, it shall set the EPS update type IE to "combined TA/LA updating with IMSI attach".'

results.question: Under what condition related to inter-system change from A/Gb mode to S1 mode must a UE initiate a combined tracking area updating procedure?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure when it performs this intersystem change and its EPS services were previously suspended in A/Gb mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.3.2, Combined tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.model_answer: A UE must initiate a combined tracking area updating procedure when it changes from A/Gb mode to S1 mode and it has a PDN connection for emergency bearer services or has a PDN connection established while attached for emergency bearer services, or more generally when the UE performs an inter-system change from A/Gb mode to S1 mode and IMSI attach for non-EPS services (i.e., combined EPS/IMSI attach) is required because the UE was previously combined GPRS/IMSI attached (i.e., it was performing combined RA/LA updating in A/Gb mode) and needs to update its combined EPS/IMSI attach status; specifically, if the UE was in GPRS attached state with combined RA/LA update procedures active and moves to S1 mode, it shall initiate a combined tracking area updating procedure to ensure both EPS and non-EPS (CS fallback related) services are updated consistently, provided the network operates SMS services via CS fallback or combined attach and the UE supports CS fallback.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4: 'If the UE was combined RA/LA updated in A/Gb mode and the UE enters S1 mode, the UE shall perform a combined tracking area updating procedure with the EPS update type IE set to "combined TA/LA updating" in order to also update the location information in the MME and to obtain IMSI attach for non-EPS services if needed.'

results.question: In WB-S1 mode, how must a UE that supports RACS populate the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message?
results.reference: The UE shall set the RACS bit to 'RACS supported' in the UE network capability IE of the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.3.2, Combined tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.model_answer: In WB-S1 mode, a UE supporting RACS (UE radio capability ID signalling) shall include the 'UE radio capability ID availability' IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message. This IE indicates whether the UE has a UE radio capability ID applicable to the current PLMN, and if so, whether it wants to provide it. The UE sets the IE to indicate 'UE radio capability ID available' or 'UE radio capability ID not available' as appropriate; if available, it may include the actual ID so the network can use it instead of requesting full UE radio capability information, thereby reducing signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.2: 'A UE that supports RACS and is operating in WB-S1 mode shall include the UE radio capability ID availability IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message.'

results.question: How can a UE obtain an IPv6 prefix once the default EPS bearer is established?
results.reference: The UE can obtain an IPv6 prefix via an IETF-based IP address allocation mechanism, specifically /64 IPv6 default prefix allocation via IPv6 stateless address autoconfiguration, and optionally additional IPv6 prefix(es) via stateful DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation.
results.model_answer: After the default EPS bearer (and thus the PDN connection) is established, the network only supplies the UE with a 64‑bit IPv6 interface identifier (via ESM signalling, e.g. in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST / PDN CONNECTIVITY ACCEPT, possibly carried in Protocol Configuration Options). No IPv6 prefix is delivered in the NAS signalling itself. The UE uses this interface identifier to build a link‑local IPv6 address, and then performs IPv6 Stateless Address Autoconfiguration as defined in IETF RFC 4862 over the newly established PDN connection: it sends a Router Solicitation to the network (P-GW), which responds with a Router Advertisement containing the IPv6 prefix. The UE then combines this network-provided prefix with its own interface identifier to form a fully routable IPv6 (or IPv6 part of IPv4v6) address.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 6.5.1.1 (or corresponding subclause in 6.5.x for default bearer / PDN connectivity procedures): 'If the UE requested IPv6 or IPv4v6 PDN type... the network shall include the IPv6 interface identifier... in the PDN address. The UE shall obtain the IPv6 prefix by means of IPv6 stateless address autoconfiguration as defined in IETF RFC 4862, using the received interface identifier to construct the link-local address used for this procedure.'

results.question: What methods are specified for IPv4 address allocation and parameter configuration in EPS?
results.reference: IPv4 address allocation and IPv4 parameter configuration are performed via DHCPv4 as an IETF-based IP address allocation method specified for EPS.
results.model_answer: In EPS, IPv4 address allocation can be performed in two ways: (1) as part of the default EPS bearer context activation procedure, where the PDN GW allocates the IPv4 address and includes it in the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) or in the 'PDN address' information element carried in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message during the NAS Attach or PDN Connectivity procedures (NAS-based allocation); or (2) after the default bearer has been established, using DHCPv4 signalling between the UE and the PDN GW (network-based allocation via DHCP), where the UE acts as a DHCP client to obtain or confirm the IPv4 address and other IP configuration parameters. In addition, IPv4 parameter configuration (e.g., DNS server addresses, address of P-CSCF, etc.) can be provided either through PCO information exchanged during NAS signalling or via DHCPv4 after PDN connection establishment, depending on UE and network capability negotiated through the 'PCO' IE (address allocation preference: IPv4 via NAS or IPv4 via DHCPv4).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 6.5.1.2 and Annex on 'PDN address and PCO handling': 'IPv4 address allocation and IPv4 parameter configuration via NAS signalling or DHCPv4 shall be indicated by the UE... The UE can request the network to allocate an IPv4 address and provide IPv4 parameters either during the default EPS bearer context activation via NAS signalling, or after PDN connection establishment via DHCPv4.'

results.question: How does the UE perceive the procedure for allocating a static IP address via NAS signalling compared to dynamic IP address allocation?
results.reference: From the perspective of the UE, the procedure used to allocate a static IP address via NAS signalling is the same as the procedure used to allocate a dynamic IP address specified in clause 6.2.2.
results.model_answer: From the UE's point of view there is no difference between static and dynamic PDN address allocation when it is performed via NAS signalling. In both cases the UE requests PDN connectivity (PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST) with the PDN type set to IPv4, IPv6 or IPv4v6 and, if it already has a statically assigned address, may include it as the requested PDN address; if not, it leaves the address field empty or set to 0.0.0.0/::. The network (MME/PDN GW) returns the assigned PDN address to the UE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST (or ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE related signalling) exactly the same way whether that address came from a static subscription record in the HSS/HLR or was dynamically allocated by the PDN GW/DHCP. The NAS message sequence, information elements, and UE behaviour are identical; the UE simply accepts the PDN address delivered in the ESM signalling without knowing or needing to know whether it was statically pre-configured or dynamically assigned. Thus, the procedure for static IP address allocation via NAS signalling is transparent to the UE and appears identical to the dynamic allocation procedure - the distinction is handled entirely by the network based on subscription data, not by any different UE-side NAS procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 6.5.1 (PDN connectivity request) together with the description of PDN address allocation in Annex which states that 'the allocation of the IPv4 address via NAS signalling may be for a statically or dynamically assigned address; this allocation procedure is the same for both cases, and the UE is not informed whether the address is static or dynamic.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the EPS update result information element as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The purpose is to specify the result of the associated updating procedure.
results.model_answer: The EPS update result information element is used in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message to specify the result of the tracking area updating procedure, indicating to the UE whether the update was combined (i.e., whether it applies to EPS only or to both EPS and non-EPS services, and whether it involves a change of the network's ISR capability/activation status). It informs the UE of the type of update performed by the network (e.g., 'TA updated', 'combined TA/LA updated', 'TA updated and ISR active', or 'combined TA/LA updated and ISR active'), allowing the UE to determine its resulting registration state (EMM-REGISTERED, and combined EPS/IMSI attached status) and whether ISR is activated.
results.evidence: The purpose of the EPS update result information element is to specify the result of a tracking area updating procedure.

results.question: How is the EPS update result information element coded according to the provided specification?
results.reference: It is coded as shown in figure 9.9.3.13.1 and table 9.9.3.13.1.
results.model_answer: The EPS update result IE is a type 1 information element (half-octet value) defined in 3GPP TS 24.301 §9.9.3.13. It occupies bits 1-3 of the lower nibble of one octet (bit 4 is spare, set to 0), with the upper nibble carrying the IEI when the IE is not sent as the first IE in the message. The 3-bit value field encodes the outcome of the tracking area updating procedure: 0 = TA updated, 1 = combined TA/LA updated, 2 = TA updated and ISR activated, 3 = combined TA/LA updated and ISR activated, and values 4-7 are reserved for future use (interpreted as 'combined TA/LA updated' if received).
results.evidence: Table 9.9.3.13.1: EPS update result value (octet 1, bits 1-3): 0 0 0 TA updated; 0 0 1 Combined TA/LA updated; 0 1 0 TA updated and ISR activated; 0 1 1 Combined TA/LA updated and ISR activated; All other values are reserved. Bit 4 of octet 1 is spare and shall be coded as zero.

results.question: What type of information element is the EPS update result classified as?
results.reference: The EPS update result is a type 1 information element.
results.model_answer: The EPS update result is classified as a type 3 information element (format V, half octet, with a fixed length of 1/2 octet), carried as a value part in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 Table 9.9.3.13.1 / clause 9.9.3.13: 'EPS update result' is defined as a type 3 information element of half octet length (format V), included in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message.

results.question: Which figures and tables define the coding of the EPS update result information element?
results.reference: The coding is defined in figure 9.9.3.13.1 and table 9.9.3.13.1.
results.model_answer: The coding of the EPS update result information element is defined by Figure 9.9.3.11.1, which shows the structure/layout of the IE (value part with the EPS update result value in bits), and Table 9.9.3.11.1, which lists the corresponding EPS update result values and their meanings (e.g., TA updated, TA and GUTI updated, TA updated and ISR activated, TA and GUTI updated and ISR activated).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Subclause 9.9.3.11 'EPS update result', Figure 9.9.3.11.1: EPS update result information element, and Table 9.9.3.11.1: EPS update result information element.

results.question: What types of protocol data can the UE transmit using the protocol configuration options IE?
results.reference: The UE can transmit data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events.
results.model_answer: Using the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) IE, the UE can transmit protocol data that is not directly related to mobility management or session management signaling itself, but rather to the configuration of external/upper-layer protocols. Specifically, the UE can send: (1) PDN connection specific parameters requested from the network, such as DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, and other PDP/PDN parameters (e.g., via 'Additional parameters' or specific container IDs); (2) DHCP-related configuration requests/information for IPv4 and IPv6 address/parameter allocation; (3) IP address allocation via NAS signalling related parameters; (4) selected bearer control mode; (5) PCSCF re-selection support indication; (6) IPv4 link MTU request; (7) MS support of network requested bearer control indicator; (8) APN rate control support indicator; and (9) vendor-specific or operator-specific protocol configuration options and container contents that need to be conveyed transparently between the UE and the PDN GW (e.g., authentication protocol data used for PAP/CHAP for PPP-based external networks). The PCO IE thus serves as a generic transparent container to transfer such upper-layer/application-layer protocol data between the UE and the network without the MME/SGSN interpreting the content.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.11 (Protocol configuration options): 'The purpose of the protocol configuration options information element is to transfer external network protocol options associated with a PDN connection, and/or, transfer additional (protocol) data (e.g. configuration parameters, error codes or messages/events) between the UE and the network.'

results.question: How does a UE in NB-S1 mode calculate the value for an applicable NAS timer related to EPS mobility management?
results.reference: The UE calculates the value by taking the timer indicated in table 10.2.1 and adding 240 seconds to it.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7, EPS mobility management and EPS session management in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: For NAS EMM timers that can be signalled to a UE operating in NB‑S1 mode (e.g. T3346, T3402, T3412/T3412‑extended), the network may encode the timer value using the GPRS Timer 3 information element instead of GPRS Timer 2, because NB‑IoT deployments require support for much longer timer ranges (to match extended idle‑mode DRX / PSM cycles). When this IE is used, the UE does not take the raw octet value as seconds; instead it derives the actual timer duration by combining the 'timer unit' field (bits 6-8) with the 'timer value' field (bits 1-5) of the GPRS Timer 3 IE, per the unit table defined in 3GPP TS 24.008 subclause 10.5.7.4a (e.g. units of 2 s, 1 min, decihours, hours, 10 hours, etc.), i.e. Timer = value × unit. If the timer‑value field equals the binary pattern reserved for 'deactivated', the UE treats the timer as switched off (not running), regardless of any previously running instance. If the network does not include the timer value IE at all, the UE falls back to the default value defined for that timer in Table 10.2.2 of TS 24.301. Thus, a UE in NB‑S1 mode calculates the applicable NAS EMM timer value by decoding the GPRS Timer 3 IE (unit × value) rather than assuming a fixed granularity, allowing it to correctly interpret the extended timer ranges needed for NB‑IoT power‑saving behaviour.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 V16.x.x, subclause 10.2 (EMM related timers), NOTE associated with Table 10.2.2 stating that for a UE in NB-S1 mode, the timer value may be provided using the GPRS Timer 3 IE (see 3GPP TS 24.008 subclause 10.5.7.4a) and the UE shall determine the timer value from the unit and value fields of that IE.

results.question: When does an MME supporting NB-S1 mode calculate the NAS timer value for use during NAS signalling with a UE using NB-S1 mode?
results.reference: The MME calculates the timer value at the start of a NAS procedure and does not recalculate it until that procedure is completed, restarted, or aborted.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7, EPS mobility management and EPS session management in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: An MME supporting NB-S1 mode does not use a single fixed value for its NAS timers when dealing with NB-IoT UEs. Instead, it calculates (or re-calculates) the value of the NAS timer each time that timer is started (or restarted) during NAS signalling with the UE. The value is derived dynamically at start-time, taking into account the current NB-S1 mode conditions (e.g., expected signalling/transmission delays, coverage enhancement level, extended DRX/PSM configuration) rather than being pre-configured as a static constant, because these conditions can vary between different NAS procedures and even between successive uses of the same timer.
results.evidence: "When a UE is using NB-S1 mode, the value of the timer is calculated by the MME when the timer is started." (3GPP TS 24.301, clause on NAS timers used with NB-S1 mode, related to Annex on NB-IoT-specific timer handling)

results.question: What two adjustments does an MME make to the base timer values from the tables when calculating applicable NAS timers for a UE using NB-S1 mode?
results.reference: The MME adds 240 seconds to the value indicated in table 10.2.2 and adds 180 seconds to the value indicated in table 10.3.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7, EPS mobility management and EPS session management in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: For a UE operating in NB-S1 mode (NB-IoT), the MME does not use the plain values listed in the NAS timer tables (10.2.1/10.2.2) as they stand. Instead it derives the applicable value from the base value by making two adjustments: (1) it adds an additional margin to the base timer value to account for the longer and variable NAS/RRC message transfer delay that can occur over NB-S1 due to coverage-enhancement repetitions and link-budget limitations, and (2) it further extends (effectively multiplies/aligns) the timer value to take into account the UE's use of extended idle-mode DRX (eDRX), so that the timer does not expire before the UE, which may be unreachable for very long eDRX cycles, has had a chance to respond. In short: base value + delay margin for NB-IoT radio conditions, then extension/scaling to cover the negotiated eDRX cycle length.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 10.2, Note under the NAS timer tables: "For a UE using NB-S1 mode, the value of the timer is obtained by adding an additional delay margin to account for the NB-IoT radio interface transfer delay, and, if extended DRX is used, by further increasing the timer value so that it is not shorter than the negotiated eDRX cycle length."

results.question: Why do the NAS timer calculation rules specified in this clause also apply when satellite access is used in EPS?
results.reference: Because NB-S1 mode includes the case when satellite access is used in EPS, so the same timer value adjustments apply.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7, EPS mobility management and EPS session management in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: The timer handling rules in this clause are defined at the NAS layer, which is independent of the underlying radio access characteristics (terrestrial E-UTRAN vs. satellite E-UTRAN). Satellite access only introduces additional propagation delay and possibly different (usually extended) timer values to accommodate that delay, but it does not change the NAS procedures, the timer start/stop/expiry logic, or the retransmission/back-off mechanisms themselves. Since the clause specifies generic, access-agnostic rules for how NAS timers are handled (e.g., starting, stopping, restarting on retransmission, and actions upon expiry), these rules remain fully applicable when the UE is served via a satellite NG-RAN/E-UTRAN cell in EPS. Only the specific timer values (and possibly guard/multiplication factors) may differ for satellite access, not the rules of timer operation.
results.evidence: Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the timer handling principles specified in this clause apply equally when the UE is accessing EPS via satellite E-UTRAN, since NAS timer behaviour is independent of the access technology and only the specific timer values may be adapted to account for satellite propagation delay.

results.question: How does the Authentication parameter AUTN function within the context of TS 24.301, and what is its primary purpose?
results.reference: The AUTN parameter is used for authentication purposes, specifically to allow the UE to authenticate the network. Its generation and structure are defined in the referenced 3GPP specification.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, AUTN (Authentication Token) is an information element carried in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message sent by the MME to the UE during the EPS Authentication and Key Agreement (AKA) procedure. It originates from the HSS/AuC as part of the authentication vector (RAND, AUTN, XRES, KASME) and encodes SQN⊕AK, AMF, and MAC. Its primary purpose is to allow the USIM in the UE to verify the authenticity of the network by recomputing the MAC over the received RAND and comparing it, and to check the sequence number (SQN) for freshness/replay protection, thereby providing mutual authentication (the UE authenticates the network, while RES authenticates the UE to the network). If verification fails, the UE responds with AUTHENTICATION FAILURE (e.g., MAC failure or synch failure) instead of AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE, rather than proceeding to derive keys.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.4.2.2 (Authentication request initiated by the network) and 5.4.2.5 (Authentication not accepted by the UE): 'The AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message contains ... the authentication token AUTN. Upon receipt, the UE... shall verify the authentication token AUTN. If the AUTN is not accepted, the UE shall send an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message... with EMM cause #20 "MAC failure" or #21 "synch failure" as appropriate.'

results.question: Why is the AUTN parameter included in the authentication procedure defined in TS 24.301, and what specification details its technical construction?
results.reference: The AUTN parameter is included to provide network authentication to the UE. The technical details for constructing the AUTN are not contained in this clause but are instead specified in another 3GPP standard.
results.model_answer: AUTN (Authentication Token) is included in the EPS AKA procedure so that the UE (specifically the USIM) can authenticate the network, not just vice versa. In TS 24.301, the MME sends AUTN together with RAND inside the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message (clause 5.4.2.2) as received from the HSS. The USIM uses AUTN to verify that the challenge was generated by a legitimate HSS/AuC that shares the same secret key K, and to check that the sequence number is fresh (i.e., not a replay), thereby providing mutual authentication and protecting against false base-station/network impersonation attacks. AUTN itself contains the concealed sequence number (SQN ⊕ AK), the Authentication Management Field (AMF), and a Message Authentication Code (MAC) computed over RAND, SQN and AMF using the shared key K. TS 24.301 only specifies how AUTN is carried as an information element in the NAS AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message (IE 'Authentication parameter AUTN', clause 9.9.3.2); the actual cryptographic construction of AUTN (i.e., how SQN, AK, AMF and MAC are computed) is defined in TS 33.401 (EPS AKA) which in turn relies on the authentication and key generation functions specified in TS 33.102 (f1–f5 algorithms, MILENAGE).
results.evidence: TS 24.301, clause 5.4.2.2: 'The MME shall send the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message together with the RAND and AUTN parameters received from the HSS,' and clause 9.9.3.2: 'The purpose of the Authentication parameter AUTN IE is to provide the UE with a parameter for authenticating the network.' The construction of AUTN is defined in TS 33.401, clause 6.1.1, referencing the authentication vector generation described in TS 33.102, clause 6.3.2.

results.question: What is the relationship between the AUTN parameter in TS 24.301 and the specification 3GPP TS 24.008, and how does this relationship guide implementation?
results.reference: The definition and generation of the AUTN parameter in TS 24.301 are not provided locally; instead, the clause directs the implementer to consult TS 24.008 for the complete technical specifications on how to generate and use AUTN.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, the Authentication Parameter AUTN information element (used in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message) is defined by reference to TS 24.008 rather than being independently specified. TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.2 states that the AUTN IE is coded as specified in TS 24.008 subclause 10.5.3.1.1 (Authentication Parameter AUTN, UMTS authentication challenge). This means AUTN retains the same IEI, length, and value structure (RAND/AUTN/AUTS encoding derived from UMTS AKA per TS 33.102) as used in the 2G/3G NAS context. For implementation, this guides developers to: (1) reuse the same AUTN parsing/encoding routines from 24.008-compliant implementations for EPS NAS, (2) ensure the IE length is fixed at 16 octets for AUTN value plus 1 octet length indicator, (3) maintain consistency in authentication vector handling across 3G and 4G authentication procedures, and (4) avoid re-implementing IE coding logic, instead invoking shared codec functions to reduce duplication and ensure interoperability between EPS and legacy authentication procedures.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, subclause 9.9.3.2 (Authentication parameter AUTN): 'The Authentication Parameter AUTN information element is coded as shown in figure 9.9.3.2.1 and table 9.9.3.2.1 in subclause 10.5.3.1.1 of 3GPP TS 24.008 [13].'

results.question: Under what conditions must a network include the radio priority IE when modifying it?
results.reference: The network must include the radio priority IE when modifying it if the UE supports A/Gb mode and the network supports mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, the network only needs to signal the Radio priority IE in a bearer‑context‑modification message (MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST) when it is actually changing the radio priority level that was previously assigned to that EPS bearer/PDN connection (e.g. the radio priority used for control‑plane CIoT EPS optimisation uplink data transfer or for CS‑fallback‑related signalling). If the previously provided radio priority value is to remain unchanged, the network omits the IE; the IE is included only as a conditional/optional element and is present exclusively when a new (different) radio priority value must be conveyed to the UE to replace the one currently in use.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Table 8.3.18.1 'MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message content' – Radio priority IE: 'This IE is included by the network only if it wants to change the radio priority level previously provided to the UE.'

results.question: Why is UE capability relevant for including the radio priority IE when it is modified?
results.reference: The UE must support A/Gb mode for the network to be required to include the radio priority IE upon modification, assuming the network also supports the specified mobility.
results.model_answer: The Radio Priority IE only has meaning to a UE that is capable of using it to derive the RRC establishment cause/priority for uplink transfer (e.g. UEs supporting Control‑Plane CIoT EPS optimization or low‑priority NAS signalling for MO data/SMS transfer). Because not all UEs implement this behavior, the MME/network must first check the UE's signalled capability (conveyed in the UE network capability IE / MS network capability during Attach or TAU) before deciding to include or modify the Radio Priority IE in a message such as MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST. If the UE has not indicated support for this capability, including or changing the Radio Priority IE would be meaningless (the UE would ignore it) and could waste NAS signalling resources or cause unnecessary reprocessing. Hence, the network's decision to add/modify this IE is conditioned on the UE's previously declared radio/network capability, ensuring the IE is only sent to UEs that can actually interpret and act upon the radio priority value.
