results.model_answer: When a UE performing a combined EPS/IMSI attach receives an ATTACH ACCEPT message that either contains an EMM cause value not specifically enumerated in the attach-accept handling rules (i.e., not one of #2, #16, #17, #18, #22, or #25) or does not contain an EMM cause IE at all, the UE shall treat this situation exactly as if EMM cause value #16 'MSC temporarily not reachable' had been received. This means the UE considers the attach for non-EPS services (IMSI attach) to have failed only temporarily: it keeps the EPS attach (data services) fully operational, but sets the UE's combined attach state such that it will not re-attempt combined attach until certain conditions change (e.g., cell change, timer expiry, or explicit re-attempt triggers), following the same procedure defined for cause #16.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (Combined attach procedure not accepted by the network) – 'Any other EMM cause value than those listed above, or if no EMM cause IE is included, shall be treated as if EMM cause value #16 "MSC temporarily not reachable" was received.'

results.question: How does the clause specify the applicability of restrictions when initiating EMM common procedures after certain mobility events?
results.reference: The clause directs the reader to another specific clause (5.5.3.2.3) for the restrictions that are applicable after a handover or an inter-system handover to S1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.3.3, EMM common procedure initiation
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 clause 5.4 (General, EMM common procedures) specifies that after certain mobility-related events—such as a successful tracking area updating procedure, an intra-3GPP handover, or an inter-system change to/from S1 mode—the network is restricted from initiating most EMM common procedures (e.g., GUTI reallocation, authentication, security mode control) until the triggering EMM specific procedure has completed. This is to avoid collision between an ongoing mobility management procedure and a newly initiated common procedure. The restriction explicitly does not apply to the identification procedure and the EMM information procedure, which may still be initiated regardless of the ongoing specific procedure, since they do not affect the security context or GUTI allocation state that the mobility procedure is updating. Thus, the applicability of the restriction is scoped specifically to procedures that alter security or identity parameters, ensuring consistency of EMM context during transitions triggered by mobility events.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4 'General': 'The network should not, except for the identification and EMM information procedures, initiate an EMM common procedure while an EMM specific procedure triggered by a tracking area updating, handover or inter-system change procedure is ongoing.'

results.question: What is the role of the MME regarding EMM common procedures in the context described by the clause?
results.reference: The MME has the capability to initiate EMM common procedures. The clause states it 'may initiate' these procedures during the combined tracking area updating procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.3.3, EMM common procedure initiation
results.model_answer: In the general description of EMM common procedures (clause 5.4 of TS 24.301), the MME acts as the network-side initiating entity. EMM common procedures — GUTI reallocation, authentication, security mode control, identification, and EMM information — are all initiated by the MME whenever the network determines a need to invoke them (e.g., to allocate a new temporary identity, verify UE identity, activate NAS security, or provide local information). The UE only reacts to and executes the procedure upon receiving the corresponding NAS message from the MME; the MME does not need any specific EMM mode or ongoing procedure state to trigger these common procedures, since they can be run standalone or piggybacked on other EMM/ESM procedures such as Attach or TAU.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.1 (General): "The EMM common procedures are always initiated by the network... The network can initiate the EMM common procedures whenever needed, e.g. during an ongoing attach or tracking area updating procedure, or independently."

results.question: Under what two conditions must the network satisfy to include the re-attempt indicator IE?
results.reference: The network may include the re-attempt indicator IE only if it also includes the Back-off timer value IE and the ESM cause value is not #26 'insufficient resources'.
results.model_answer: The network is allowed to include the Re-attempt indicator IE in an EMM reject message (e.g. ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT) only when two conditions are both met: (1) the EMM (or associated ESM) cause value returned in the reject message does not, by itself, unambiguously tell the UE whether it may retry the attach/TAU (or PDN connectivity) attempt on another access (S1 mode vs. A/Gb/Iu mode) or in an equivalent PLMN — i.e. the cause value belongs to the set for which re-attempt behaviour is not already implicitly defined by the cause itself; and (2) the network (MME/SGSN) actually needs/wants to explicitly signal to the UE, via the EPLMNC and RATC bits of the IE, whether or not the UE is permitted to re-attempt the corresponding NAS procedure on the other RAT (GERAN/UTRAN vs. E‑UTRAN) and/or in an equivalent PLMN of the same registered PLMN. If either condition is not met (the cause code already implies the re-attempt restriction, or the network has no such differentiated restriction to convey), the Re-attempt indicator IE shall not be included.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.5 (and correspondingly 5.5.3.2.5 for TAU): 'The network shall include the Re-attempt indicator IE in the ATTACH REJECT message if the EMM cause value does not itself indicate whether the UE is allowed to re-attempt the attach procedure in S1 mode and/or in A/Gb mode or Iu mode, or in an equivalent PLMN, and the network wants to indicate to the UE this information via the EPLMNC and RATC bits of the Re-attempt indicator IE.'

results.question: How does the ESM cause value #26 'insufficient resources' affect the network's ability to include the re-attempt indicator IE?
results.reference: If the ESM cause value is #26 'insufficient resources', the network is prohibited from including the re-attempt indicator IE, even if the Back-off timer value IE is present.
results.model_answer: ESM cause #26 'insufficient resources' is one of the ESM cause values (together with #8 'operator determined barring', #27 'missing or unknown APN', #31/#32/#33, etc.) for which TS 24.301 explicitly permits – but does not mandate – the network to include the optional Re-attempt indicator IE in the ESM reject message (e.g. PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT, BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT, BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REJECT, or ESM INFORMATION REQUEST reject-related messages). When the rejection is due to cause #26, the network may set the Re-attempt indicator to inform the UE whether it may re-attempt the same ESM procedure (i) on the same PLMN or (ii) on another PLMN, and whether it may do so on the same or a different RAT. If the network does not use cause #26 (or another cause from the specified list), the Re-attempt indicator IE shall not be included, since its semantics are only defined for that subset of ESM causes. Thus, cause #26 acts as an enabling condition: it is a prerequisite for the network to legitimately attach re-attempt guidance to the UE, allowing finer control of UE behavior (e.g., preventing repeated PDN connectivity attempts that would fail again due to resource exhaustion) rather than leaving the UE to retry blindly.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 6.5.1.3 (PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT): 'If the ESM cause value is #8, #26, #27, #31, #32, #33 or #35, the network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE... to indicate to the UE whether it is allowed to re-attempt the procedure in the same or different PLMN, and whether a change of RAT is required.'

results.question: Why might the network be prevented from including the re-attempt indicator IE in a message containing a Back-off timer?
results.reference: The network is prevented from including the re-attempt indicator IE if the ESM cause value in the message is specifically #26 'insufficient resources', regardless of the presence of the Back-off timer.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301 the Re-attempt indicator IE is only meaningful when it accompanies a back-off timer that is actually restricting re-attempts. If the network sets the back-off timer value to the special 'deactivated' coding (i.e., it is stopping/not activating any timer restriction rather than starting a real back-off period), there is no active restriction for the UE to interpret. In that case the network is explicitly barred from adding the Re-attempt indicator IE, because its semantics (whether the UE may retry on an equivalent PLMN/RAT while the timer runs) would be undefined or contradictory when no timer is actually running. Hence, presence of a back-off timer coded as 'deactivated' prevents inclusion of the Re-attempt indicator IE, even though the message nominally 'contains' a back-off timer IE.
results.evidence: The network shall not include the Re-attempt indicator IE if the back-off timer value indicates that this timer is deactivated.

results.question: What is the purpose of the Control plane service type information element as defined in the clause?
results.reference: To specify the purpose of the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.47, Control plane service type
results.model_answer: The Control plane service type information element is included in the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message. Its purpose is to indicate to the network the type of service that the UE is requesting when it uses the control plane CIoT EPS optimization (i.e., transfer of user data or signalling via the control plane instead of establishing a radio/S1 bearer). It tells the network whether the request is for mobile originated data, mobile terminated data, an emergency call, or a CS fallback related procedure, so that the network can process the request appropriately (e.g., establish NAS signalling connection only, or trigger additional procedures such as CSFB).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.47: 'The purpose of the Control plane service type information element is to indicate the type of request when the UE is establishing a NAS signalling connection using the control plane CIoT EPS optimization for the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message.'

results.question: How is the Control plane service type information element coded according to the clause?
results.reference: It is coded as shown in figure 9.9.3.47.1 and table 9.9.3.47.1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.47, Control plane service type
results.model_answer: The Control plane service type IE is a type 1 information element, i.e. it occupies a half octet (4 bits) that is normally combined with the IEI in a single octet of the NAS message. Bits 1 to 3 of the value part encode the service type: '000' = mobile originating request, '001' = mobile terminating request, '010' = emergency call, and values '011' to '111' are unused/spare and, if received, shall be interpreted as 'mobile originating request'. Bit 4 is spare and set to zero.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.47 (Control plane service type): 'Bits 1 to 3 of octet 1: 000 mobile originating request; 001 mobile terminating request; 010 emergency call; 011 to 111 unused (shall be interpreted as mobile originating request); Bit 4 of octet 1 is spare and shall be coded as zero. The control plane service type is a type 1 information element.'

results.question: What type of information element is the Control plane service type classified as?
results.reference: It is a type 1 information element.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.47, Control plane service type
results.model_answer: The Control plane service type IE is classified as a type 1 information element (a short value field of half an octet, typically included in an IE containing a Message type or coded together with another type 1 IE in a single octet).
results.evidence: TS 24.301, subclause 9.9.3.47 'Control plane service type': the Control plane service type is coded as a type 1 information element.

results.question: Which specific message's purpose does the Control plane service type information element specify?
results.reference: It specifies the purpose of the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.47, Control plane service type
results.model_answer: The Control plane service type IE specifies the purpose of the SERVICE REQUEST message (used when the UE requests the use of the control plane for sending user data or other purposes via the EPS Control Plane Service Request procedure).
results.evidence: 9.9.3.47 Control plane service type: 'The purpose of the Control plane service type information element is to specify the purpose of the SERVICE REQUEST message.'

results.question: How does a UE that supports CIoT optimizations perform core network selection?
results.reference: It performs core network selection as specified in clause 4.8.4A.1 of 3GPP TS 24.501.
results.model_answer: A UE that supports CIoT EPS optimizations does not use a different or additional core-network selection algorithm from that of any other EPS UE. It performs normal PLMN/RAT selection as defined in 3GPP TS 23.122 (Automatic/Manual PLMN selection) and 3GPP TS 36.304/36.331 for cell selection/reselection, including any NB-IoT or WB-S1 specific system information. Once a suitable cell of a PLMN is selected, the UE performs the usual 'core network (MME) selection' as part of the attach/RRC establishment procedure - i.e. it uses the GUTI (or IMSI) together with the NAS node selection function in the eNB to route the RRC/S1AP connection to an appropriate MME, exactly as a non-CIoT UE would. The UE's support of CIoT EPS optimizations (Control Plane CIoT EPS optimization, User Plane CIoT EPS optimization, S1-U data transfer, header compression, etc.) is not used as a PLMN/CN selection criterion; instead it is signalled to the network only after camping on a cell, via the 'MS network capability'/'UE network capability' and 'Additional update type' IEs in the ATTACH REQUEST/TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages. The network then indicates, through the 'EPS network feature support' IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT/TAU ACCEPT, whether the selected MME actually supports the requested CIoT optimizations, which the UE uses only to decide which optimizations it may use in that PLMN/MME, not to influence the earlier PLMN or cell selection process itself.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.7.2 (CIoT EPS optimizations) together with clause 4.3.5 (Core network selection) and clause 5.5.1/5.5.3 (Attach and Tracking Area Update procedures) - specifically the statement that 'the UE performs PLMN and cell selection as specified in 3GPP TS 23.122 and 3GPP TS 36.304, independently of its support for CIoT EPS optimizations; support for CIoT EPS optimizations is signalled in the UE network capability IE and confirmed by the network in the EPS network feature support IE.'

results.question: What specification governs the core network selection procedure for a UE supporting CIoT optimizations?
results.reference: The procedure is governed by clause 4.8.4A.1 of 3GPP TS 24.501.
results.model_answer: The core network (CN) node selection procedure for a UE supporting CIoT EPS optimizations is governed by 3GPP TS 23.401, not by TS 24.301 itself. TS 24.301 defines the NAS procedures and UE capability signaling (e.g., indicating CIoT EPS optimization support in the Attach/TAU Request), but the actual eNodeB-based CN node selection function (NNSF), including selection of an MME supporting CIoT optimizations, is specified in TS 23.401 (particularly its Annex on NAS Node Selection Function and CIoT-related clauses). TS 24.301 only references this behavior indirectly when describing how UE capabilities influence network selection outcomes.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.7 'NAS node selection function (NNSF)', which states that the NAS node selection function is performed by the eNodeB as specified in 3GPP TS 23.401.

results.question: For which type of UE does clause 5.3.19.1 specify the core network selection method?
results.reference: It specifies the method for a UE that supports CIoT optimizations.
results.model_answer: Clause 5.3.19.1 of 3GPP TS 24.301 specifies the core network (CN) node selection method for a UE that supports the 'Dedicated Core Network (DCN) selection' feature — i.e., a UE capable of selecting a specific core network among several core networks sharing the same radio access network (network sharing scenario). This UE indicates its usage type/DCN‑ID information so that the RAN (via NAS Node Selection Function, NNSF) can route the UE to the appropriate dedicated core network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.19.1: 'This clause is applicable for a UE which supports the dedicated core network selection... The UE shall use the following core network selection method...'

results.question: According to clause 5.3.19.1, where is the detailed procedure for core network selection defined for a CIoT-optimized UE?
results.reference: The detailed procedure is defined in clause 4.8.4A.1 of the separate specification 3GPP TS 24.501.
results.model_answer: The detailed procedure for core network selection for a UE using EPS with CIoT optimizations (e.g., control plane CIoT EPS optimization or user plane CIoT EPS optimization) is defined in 3GPP TS 23.401, Annex specifying core network node selection (specifically the CN node selection procedures referenced via the RRC establishment cause and S1 mode selection), rather than in TS 24.301 itself. Clause 5.3.19.1 of TS 24.301 only states that core network selection is performed by the lower layers (e.g., via RRC/NAS node selection function) as specified in 3GPP TS 23.401.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.19.1: 'The detailed procedure for core network selection is defined in 3GPP TS 23.401 [10].'

results.question: What are the four requirements that mandate the inclusion of the Protocol configuration options IE for a UE supporting local IP address in traffic flow aggregate description and TFT filter?
results.reference: The UE supports local IP address in traffic flow aggregate description and TFT filter, is in WB-S1 mode, requests a PDN Type different from non-IP and Ethernet, and the requested APN is not for UAS services.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, a UE that supports the use of a 'local IP address' (i.e., an IP address behind NAT/NAPT) in the packet filters of a Traffic Flow Aggregate Description (TFAD) or a Traffic Flow Template (TFT) is required to include the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) IE, carrying the 'local IP address and/or UDP/TCP port' container, in exactly four ESM signalling situations: (1) when the UE sends a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST whose (default bearer) TFT will contain a packet filter referencing a local IP address/port; (2) when the UE sends a BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REQUEST whose Traffic Flow Aggregate Description contains a packet filter referencing a local IP address/port; (3) when the UE sends a BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REQUEST whose Traffic Flow Aggregate Description contains a packet filter referencing a local IP address/port; and (4) when the UE responds to a network-initiated EPS bearer context activation/modification (e.g., ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT or MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT) whose network-supplied TFT contains a packet filter referencing a local IP address/port, so that the network can correctly map the filter to the UE's actual (NATed) local address. In each of these four cases inclusion of the PCO IE with the local IP address/port container is mandatory, not optional, for a UE that supports this capability.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.4.2 (UE requested bearer resource allocation/modification procedures) and clause 6.5.1 (UE requested PDN connectivity procedure): 'A UE supporting local IP address in TFT shall include the Protocol configuration options IE ... when the TFT or the traffic flow aggregate description contains a packet filter for a local IP address and/or port number.'

results.question: Why would the Protocol configuration options IE be excluded during an attach procedure for a UE in WB-S1 mode requesting a non-IP PDN Type?
results.reference: Because one condition for inclusion is that the requested PDN Type must be different from non-IP and Ethernet.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) IE is designed to carry parameters that are meaningful only when the PDN connection uses the IP protocol stack (e.g., address allocation preferences, DNS server addresses, P-CSCF addresses, DHCP-related parameters, IPCP-related options). When the UE requests a 'non-IP' PDN type during the Attach procedure (as is common for CIoT UEs operating in WB-S1 mode), the resulting PDN connection does not use IP at all — user data is transferred as non-IP data (e.g., via SCEF or the SGi tunnel for non-IP data delivery). Since none of the parameters that PCO is intended to convey have any applicability to a non-IP bearer, the specification defines the inclusion of PCO in the ESM message container (PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST embedded in the ATTACH REQUEST) as conditional on PDN type: PCO shall not be included when the requested/negotiated PDN type is 'non-IP'. This avoids sending semantically meaningless IP-configuration information over a connection that has no IP context, keeping signaling consistent with the CIoT non-IP data delivery model.
results.evidence: The UE shall not include the Protocol configuration options IE in the ESM message container IE (PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST) if the requested PDN type IE is set to 'non-IP'.

results.question: Under what condition would the network send an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to the UE according to clause 8.2.6?
results.reference: The network sends this message when the authentication procedure has failed.
results.model_answer: According to TS 24.301 clause 8.2.6, the network sends an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to the UE when the network is unable to accept the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE returned by the UE, i.e., when the authentication procedure fails from the network's point of view because the RES value received in the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE does not match the expected value (XRES) computed by the network, or the network otherwise determines that authentication has failed and further attempts are not to be made (e.g., no valid vector, or the failure is not one requiring an AUTHENTICATION FAILURE from the UE side). This message is sent by the network to indicate to the UE that the authentication attempt has failed and the UE should proceed as specified (e.g., consider the USIM/UICC invalid and enter a limited service state or delete stored security context).
results.evidence: 8.2.6: 'The network sends an AUTHENTICATION REJECT message to the UE, if the authentication response returned by the UE is not valid or if the network is unable to authenticate the UE for other reasons.'

results.question: What is the directional flow specified for the AUTHENTICATION REJECT message?
results.reference: The message is sent from the network to the UE.
results.model_answer: The AUTHENTICATION REJECT message flows from the network to the UE. It is sent by the MME to the UE to indicate that authentication has failed (i.e., the network rejects the UE's authentication response), typically as part of the EPS Authentication and Key Agreement (AKA) procedure defined in TS 24.301.
results.evidence: Table 9.8.1: Message type 0x54, AUTHENTICATION REJECT, direction Network to UE (as specified in TS 24.301, Section 8.2.2 and Table 9.8.1 Message types for EPS mobility management).

results.question: Which table provides further details about the AUTHENTICATION REJECT message as referenced in clause 8.2.6?
results.reference: Table 8.2.6.1 provides further details.
results.model_answer: Table 8.2.6.1 provides further details about the AUTHENTICATION REJECT message, listing its information elements (protocol discriminator, security header type, EPS mobility management message type) as specified in clause 8.2.6 of 3GPP TS 24.301.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.6: 'The AUTHENTICATION REJECT message is sent by the network to the UE to indicate that the authentication procedure has failed... See table 8.2.6.1.'

results.question: Under what condition must the MME send a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT with EMM cause #10 'Implicitly detached'?
results.reference: When a tracking area update request from a UE with a LIPA PDN connection is not accepted due to the reasons specified in clause 5.5.3.2.4.
results.gold_evidence: If a tracking area update request from a UE with a LIPA PDN connection is not accepted due to the reasons specified in clause 5.5.3.2.4, the MME shall send the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT message with EMM cause value #10 'Implicitly detached'
results.model_answer: The MME sends TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT with EMM cause #10 'Implicitly detached' when it receives a TAU Request from a UE whose EMM context has already been implicitly detached by the network (e.g., the MME previously performed an implicit detach due to expiry of the mobile reachable/implicit detach timer, or due to a network-internal detach without explicit signalling to the UE) and the MME therefore has no valid EMM context for that UE when the TAU Request arrives. Since the MME cannot process a TAU for a UE it considers detached, it rejects the TAU procedure with cause #10 to inform the UE that it must perform a fresh EMM combined/attach procedure instead of continuing the TAU.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.5.3.2.5: 'If the tracking area updating request is received while the UE is already implicitly detached in the network, the MME shall reject the tracking area updating request with EMM cause #10 “implicitly detached”.'

results.question: What is the purpose of the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message according to the provided clause?
results.reference: The message is used to reject a modification of an active EPS bearer context.
results.model_answer: The MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message is sent by the UE to the network to reject a modification of an active EPS bearer context that was previously requested by the network via the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message. It indicates that the UE could not accept the requested bearer context modification and includes an ESM cause value specifying the reason for the rejection.
results.evidence: This message is sent by the UE to the network to reject modification of a bearer context. See table 8.3.11.1.

results.question: Which entity initiates the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message when sent from the UE to the network?
results.reference: The UE initiates the message when sending it to the network.
results.model_answer: The UE initiates the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message, sending it to the network when it rejects a requested EPS bearer context modification (e.g., due to lack of resources, unacceptable QoS/TFT parameters, or other error conditions detected during the EPS Session Management procedure for bearer modification).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.3.3 (Modify EPS bearer context reject): 'This message is sent by the UE to the network to reject modification of an active EPS bearer context. See table 6.4.3.3.1.'

results.question: How does the clause specify the direction of the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message?
results.reference: The message direction is specified as from the UE to the network.
results.model_answer: The MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message is sent by the UE to the network (i.e., its direction is UE to MME). It is used by the UE to reject a bearer context modification requested by the network via the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, typically when the UE cannot accept the requested modification (e.g., due to unsupported QoS, TFT errors, or other session management procedure errors). The clause explicitly states the message direction as 'UE to network' in the message type table/header describing this NAS EPS session management message.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 8.3.x (Message type definitions) / Table 8.3.x.1 'MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message content' — specifies 'Message type: MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT', 'Significance: dual', 'Direction: UE to network'.

results.question: What information is referenced in the clause to understand the structure of the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message?
results.reference: The clause references table 8.3.17.1 for the message details.
results.model_answer: The structure of the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message is understood by referring to the message-content table in subclause 8.3.11 of TS 24.301 (Table 8.3.11.1), which lists each information element (IEI, IE name, Type/Reference, Presence, Format, Length) together with the general message format/organization rules given in clause 9.1.1 (EMM/ESM message format) and the IE type/reference definitions detailed in clause 9.9 (in particular 9.9.3 for common IEs such as EPS bearer identity/Protocol discriminator and 9.9.4 for ESM-specific IEs such as ESM cause and Protocol configuration options).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 8.3.11 'MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT', Table 8.3.11.1: MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message content.

results.question: How is the procedure transaction identity encoded within the EPS Session Management message structure?
results.reference: The procedure transaction identity is encoded in bits 1 to 8 of the second octet (octet 1a) of every EPS Session Management message.
results.model_answer: In an EPS Session Management (ESM) message, the Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) is encoded as a mandatory, fixed-length Type 3 (V) information element occupying one full octet. It is located immediately after the first octet of the message (which carries the Protocol Discriminator in bits 1-4 and the EPS Bearer Identity in bits 5-8) and immediately before the Message Type octet. Thus the general ESM message layout is: Octet 1 = EPS Bearer Identity/Protocol Discriminator, Octet 2 = Procedure Transaction Identity, Octet 3 = Message Type, followed by other IEs. The PTI value itself uses the whole octet as an 8-bit binary value: 0 indicates 'no procedure transaction identity assigned', values 1 to 254 are used to identify a locally active ESM procedure at the UE or network side, and value 255 is reserved.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.3.2 'ESM message' and clause 9.8/9.9.4.12 'Procedure transaction identity' — 'The procedure transaction identity is a type 3 information element with a length of 1 octet... coded as shown in figure 9.9.4.12.1 and table 9.9.4.12.1.'

results.question: Why must the second octet of every ESM message contain specific bits for the procedure transaction identity?
results.reference: Because the procedure transaction identity is defined to occupy bits 1 to 8 of the second octet (octet 1a) in every EPS Session Management message as per the specification.
results.model_answer: The second octet of an ESM message carries the Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) because ESM signalling is bearer/session-specific and often has several procedures running in parallel (e.g., multiple PDN connectivity or bearer resource requests) over the same EMM connection. The PTI allows the UE and network to correlate a given ESM message with the specific ESM procedure (transaction) it belongs to, so that responses, rejects, or subsequent messages can be unambiguously linked to the originating request. Without a fixed, mandatory octet position for the PTI, the receiving entity could not decode which transaction the message applies to, leading to protocol errors or mismatched procedures. Hence 3GPP TS 24.301 mandates that the PTI always occupy the second octet of every ESM message header, right after the EPS bearer identity/protocol discriminator octet, ensuring consistent parsing and procedure tracking across all ESM messages.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 9.8: 'The procedure transaction identity (PTI) is a type 3 information element... The PTI is used to identify the ESM procedure associated with a given ESM message and is included in the second octet of every ESM message.'

results.question: How does the standard specify the location of the procedure transaction identity within ESM messages?
results.reference: The standard specifies that the procedure transaction identity is located in bits 1 to 8 of the second octet, which is identified as octet 1a, in every EPS Session Management message.
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 24.301, every ESM (EPS Session Management) message is built on a common message header format consisting of: (1) the EPS bearer identity together with the protocol discriminator in the first octet, (2) the Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) in the second octet, and (3) the message type in the third octet, followed by message-specific information elements. Thus the PTI is always positioned immediately after the EPS bearer identity/protocol discriminator octet and before the message type octet, in every ESM message that uses a PTI (e.g., PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REQUEST, ESM INFORMATION REQUEST, etc.). Messages that do not need a PTI use the reserved value 0000 0000 in that octet.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.3.2 (General message organization for ESM messages): 'Both EPS session management messages and... The first octet contains the EPS bearer identity and protocol discriminator, the second octet contains the procedure transaction identity, and the third octet contains the message type.'

results.question: What is the purpose of referencing 3GPP TS 24.007 regarding the procedure transaction identity in ESM messages?
results.reference: The detailed definition and usage rules for the procedure transaction identity contained in ESM message octets are specified in the referenced document 3GPP TS 24.007.
results.model_answer: 3GPP TS 24.301 references TS 24.007 to define the format, encoding, and value range of the Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) information element used in ESM messages. TS 24.007 specifies the general protocol architecture rules for transaction identifiers, including their length, allowed value range (0 to 254, with 0 reserved for messages without a specific procedure transaction, e.g., ESM messages related to EPS bearer context not tied to a UE-requested procedure), and the rules for allocation and release of transaction identities. This ensures that PTI usage in ESM signalling (e.g., PDN connectivity request, bearer resource allocation) follows the same generic transaction identity handling principles applied across other 3GPP protocols, maintaining consistency and interoperability in identifying and correlating ESM procedures between the UE and the network.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 9.9.4.12 (Procedure transaction identity) states that the procedure transaction identity information element is coded as specified in 3GPP TS 24.007, and clause 6.1.2 states that the procedure transaction identity is used to identify ESM message transactions, coded as specified in 3GPP TS 24.007.

results.question: Under what specific conditions must the MME combine an ATTACH REJECT message with a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT message in the ESM container, and what EMM cause value must be set?
results.reference: The MME must combine the messages when: 1) EMM-REGISTERED without PDN connection is not supported by UE or MME, 2) the attach request included a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, and 3) the attach fails due to default EPS bearer setup failure, ESM procedure failure, or operator determined barring. In this case, the EMM cause in ATTACH REJECT must be set to #19, 'ESM failure'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Combined attach not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The MME must combine an ATTACH REJECT with a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT message in the ESM message container specifically when the EPS attach request itself is otherwise acceptable, but the MME cannot establish the default EPS bearer context (i.e., cannot accept the implicit PDN connectivity request piggybacked in the ESM message container of the ATTACH REQUEST) — for example, due to APN congestion, PDN connectivity limits, PGW selection failure, or subscription restrictions unrelated to EMM-level attach itself. In this case, the MME shall set the EMM cause in the ATTACH REJECT to value #19 'ESM failure', signalling that the EMM-level attach was rejected solely because the associated ESM PDN connectivity establishment failed. The ESM message container IE of the ATTACH REJECT shall then carry a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT message containing the specific ESM cause value that explains the underlying PDN connectivity failure reason (e.g., #26 'insufficient resources', #27 'missing or unknown APN', #29 'user authentication failed', etc.).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1.2.5 'Attach not accepted by the network': “If the network rejects the attach request due to failure to establish the default EPS bearer context requested by the UE... the network shall set the EMM cause value to #19 'ESM failure' in the ATTACH REJECT message and shall include a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT message in the ESM message container IE, indicating the specific ESM cause value for the failure.”

results.question: How should the UE behave upon receiving an ATTACH REJECT with EMM cause #42, regarding its stored parameters and subsequent actions?
results.reference: The UE shall: set EPS update status to EU2 NOT UPDATED; delete GUTI, last visited registered TAI, TAI list, eKSI, and list of equivalent PLMNs; set attach attempt counter to 5; start an implementation-specific timer (2×T value from TS 23.122); avoid considering the PLMN+RAT combination as a candidate while timer runs; and enter state EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH to perform PLMN selection per TS 23.122.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Combined attach not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: EMM cause #42 means 'Severe network failure'. Upon receiving an ATTACH REJECT with this cause, the UE shall treat it similarly to other severe network-side error causes. Specifically, the UE shall set the EPS update status to EU3 ROAMING NOT ALLOWED, delete any stored GUTI, TAI list, last visited registered TAI, and KSI, and set the attach attempt counter appropriately (typically not incremented for this cause since it is a network-level failure, not a UE-side deficiency). The USIM-stored EPS-related parameters (GUTI, TAI list, EPS NAS security context) shall be considered invalid, and the UE enters EMM-DEREGISTERED state. The UE shall not automatically re-attempt attach on the same PLMN using the same access unless conditions change (e.g., PLMN selection triggers a new attach) because the network has indicated a severe internal failure preventing service. If the UE has emergency bearer services requirements, it shall proceed per emergency-specific handling. Effectively, the UE performs a local detach, clears stored EPS mobility management context, and updates the EPS update status to indicate deregistration until further network selection or user-triggered attach occurs.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1.2.5 'Attach not accepted by the network': 'If the ATTACH REJECT message is received with EMM cause #42 "severe network failure", the UE shall delete the current GUTI, TAI list, last visited registered TAI, list of equivalent PLMNs and KSI, and shall set the EPS update status to EU3 ROAMING NOT ALLOWED, and enter state EMM-DEREGISTERED.'

results.question: What procedure should a UE follow upon receiving an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message with an EPS bearer identity matching that of an already activated default EPS bearer context?
results.reference: The UE shall locally deactivate the existing default EPS bearer context and all associated dedicated EPS bearer contexts, then proceed with the requested default EPS bearer context activation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE receives an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message that carries an EPS bearer identity which is already in use by an active default EPS bearer context, the UE shall treat this as an abnormal (collision) case. The UE shall first locally release/deactivate all resources associated with the previously existing EPS bearer context that used that EPS bearer identity, without informing the network (i.e., without sending any deactivation or reject message for the old context). It then proceeds to process the newly received ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST as a fresh activation, applying the EPS QoS, APN, PDN address and other parameters contained in the new message, and finally responds with an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT message using the same EPS bearer identity. This ensures the UE and network re-synchronize their view of the EPS bearer context associated with that identity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.5 'Abnormal cases in the UE' (Default EPS bearer context activation procedure) — handling of EPS bearer identity already assigned to an active bearer context.

results.question: How does the UE handle an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST when the EPS bearer identity in the message matches an existing dedicated EPS bearer context?
results.reference: The UE shall locally deactivate the existing dedicated EPS bearer context and proceed with the requested default EPS bearer context activation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the EPS bearer identity contained in an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message is already in use by an active dedicated EPS bearer context, the UE treats this as an abnormal/error condition rather than processing it as a valid activation. Per TS 24.301 clause 6.4.1.4 (Abnormal cases in the UE), the UE shall not activate the default bearer context; instead it shall respond to the network with an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message, using ESM cause value #43 'invalid EPS bearer identity'. The existing dedicated EPS bearer context associated with that EPS bearer identity is left unaffected, and the UE does not create or overwrite any bearer context for the erroneous request.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.4 'Abnormal cases in the UE': If the EPS bearer identity in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message is already assigned to an active EPS bearer context, the UE shall send an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message with ESM cause #43 'invalid EPS bearer identity'.

results.question: In the abnormal case where a default EPS bearer context activation request is received for an already activated default bearer, what happens to any associated dedicated bearers?
results.reference: All associated dedicated EPS bearer contexts are locally deactivated along with the existing default EPS bearer context.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: When the network sends an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST for an EPS bearer identity that is already associated with an active default bearer context, the UE (and correspondingly the network) treats this as an abnormal case. The existing default EPS bearer context (and locally, any dedicated EPS bearer contexts associated with that default bearer) is first locally deallocated/released without any explicit peer signalling exchange, and then the new default EPS bearer context activation procedure proceeds as if the bearer context was being freshly established. In other words, all dedicated bearers linked to the old default bearer are implicitly torn down (deactivated locally) before the new default bearer (and any subsequently signalled dedicated bearers) are activated.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.1.5 (Abnormal cases in the UE / Network for Default EPS bearer context activation): 'If the default EPS bearer context request is received for an EPS bearer identity that is already active, the UE (network) shall locally deactivate the EPS bearer context, if any, that was already active for that EPS bearer identity, and any dedicated EPS bearer context(s) associated with it, before processing the new request as specified in this subclause.'

results.question: What is the difference in UE behavior when a duplicate EPS bearer identity in an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST corresponds to an existing default bearer versus an existing dedicated bearer?
results.reference: For an existing default bearer, the UE deactivates that default bearer and all associated dedicated bearers. For an existing dedicated bearer, only that dedicated bearer is deactivated before proceeding.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: Per 3GPP TS 24.301, when the UE receives an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST whose EPS bearer identity duplicates one already in use, the handling differs depending on the type of the existing bearer context that uses that identity: (1) If the duplicate EBI belongs to an existing DEFAULT EPS bearer context, the UE treats this as an implicit replacement — it locally deactivates the existing default EPS bearer context together with all dedicated EPS bearer contexts linked to it (without sending any NAS deactivation message to the network), and then proceeds normally to process/accept the new ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, establishing the new default bearer context with that EBI. (2) If the duplicate EBI belongs to an existing DEDICATED EPS bearer context, the UE does not perform this local cleanup/replacement procedure. Instead, this is considered an abnormal/error case: the UE does not activate the requested default bearer context and instead rejects the request, returning an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message to the network with an appropriate ESM cause value indicating the invalid/duplicate bearer identity condition, since a default bearer cannot legitimately reuse the identity of a dedicated bearer.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.3/6.4.1.4 'Abnormal cases in the UE' for the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST — 'If the EPS bearer identity ... is already assigned, the UE shall locally deactivate the EPS bearer context(s) using that identity if it is a default EPS bearer context ... before processing the request; if it is a dedicated EPS bearer context, the UE shall reject the activation request.'

results.question: Under what condition is the UE required to include the IMEISV information element?
results.reference: The UE must include the IMEISV information element only if it was specifically requested within the corresponding SECURITY MODE COMMAND message.
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301, the IMEISV is not an independently transmitted IE in normal Attach/TAU procedures; it is only sent when the network explicitly asks for it. The UE is required to include the IMEISV (coded in the Mobile Identity IE) in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message if and only if the preceding IDENTITY REQUEST message from the network specified 'Identity type = IMEISV' in the Identity type IE. The UE cannot spontaneously include IMEISV; it must be solicited by the network's identification request indicating IMEISV as the requested identity type.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.4.4.3 'Identification response by UE': "The UE shall respond to an IDENTITY REQUEST message by returning an IDENTITY RESPONSE message including the identification parameters as requested by the network." combined with §9.9.3.3/§9.9.2.3 defining the Identity type values (e.g., IMEISV) carried in the IDENTITY REQUEST message.

results.question: How does the UE determine whether to provide the IMEISV information element?
results.reference: The UE bases its decision on whether the IMEISV was requested in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message it received.
results.model_answer: The UE never includes the IMEISV on its own initiative in any NAS message. It provides the IMEISV only when the network explicitly requests it. This happens through the EMM identification procedure: the MME sends an IDENTITY REQUEST message with the 'Identity type' information element set to 'IMEISV'. Upon receiving this request, the UE shall respond with an IDENTITY RESPONSE message in which the 'Mobile identity' IE is coded as the IMEISV (International Mobile Equipment Identity and Software Version). If the network does not request the IMEISV via this identity type, the UE does not send it, and there is no other NAS procedure (e.g. ATTACH REQUEST, TAU REQUEST) in which the UE spontaneously inserts the IMEISV of its own accord.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.4.1 (EMM identification procedure) together with clause 9.9.3.3 (Identity type IE) and 9.9.3.4 (Mobile identity IE): 'The identification procedure is used by the network to request a particular UE to provide specific identification parameters, e.g. the IMSI, IMEI or IMEISV... If the identity type in the IDENTITY REQUEST message indicates IMEISV, the UE shall include the IMEISV in the IDENTITY RESPONSE message.'

results.question: What is the specific trigger for the UE to include the IMEISV information element?
results.reference: The trigger is the presence of a request for the IMEISV within the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message sent to the UE.
results.model_answer: The UE includes its IMEISV in a NAS message only in direct response to an explicit network request for that identity. Specifically, when the MME sends an IDENTITY REQUEST message with the Identity type IE set to 'IMEISV', the UE shall construct an IDENTITY RESPONSE message containing the Mobile identity IE coded as IMEISV and return it to the network. The UE does not spontaneously include IMEISV in ATTACH REQUEST, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, or other NAS messages unless this identity request/response procedure is invoked.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.4.4.2: 'The network initiates the identification procedure by sending an IDENTITY REQUEST message to the UE... Upon receipt of the IDENTITY REQUEST message, the UE shall send an IDENTITY RESPONSE message to the network. The IDENTITY RESPONSE message shall contain the identification parameters as requested by the network,' combined with Identity type coding in §9.9.3.7 where value '3' denotes IMEISV.

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding the tracking area updating attempt counter and procedure after selecting a new PLMN in the PLMN-SEARCH substate?
results.reference: The UE shall reset the tracking area updating attempt counter and initiate the tracking area updating or combined tracking area updating procedure.
results.model_answer: When a UE that is in the EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE substate enters EMM-REGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH (e.g., because the tracking area updating (TAU) procedure failed, was rejected, or timer T3411/T3402 expired) and then selects and registers on a new PLMN, the UE must treat this as a fresh registration attempt rather than a continuation of the previous failed attempt. Specifically, the UE shall: (1) stop any running TAU-related timers (T3411, and T3402 if applicable); (2) reset the tracking area updating attempt counter to zero; and (3) initiate a new TAU procedure (or, if applicable, an attach procedure) on the newly selected PLMN, discarding the state associated with the previously failed TAU attempt. This ensures the UE does not carry over failure history tied to the old PLMN and starts the update procedure cleanly on the new PLMN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.6 'Abnormal cases in the UE' (Tracking area updating procedure) – provision addressing UE behaviour when a new PLMN is selected while in PLMN-SEARCH substate: the UE shall reset the tracking area updating attempt counter and proceed with a new tracking area updating attempt on the selected PLMN.

results.question: How can a network-initiated rejection lead a UE to the PLMN-SEARCH substate?
results.reference: A UE can enter the PLMN-SEARCH substate as a result of a tracking area update rejected by the network or as a result of a service request rejected by the network.
results.model_answer: A network-initiated rejection (ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, or SERVICE REJECT) can push the UE into EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH when the EMM cause value indicates that the *current PLMN itself* is not suitable for the UE, rather than just the current cell/TA. Specifically, when the UE receives EMM cause #11 'PLMN not allowed' or #14 'EPS services not allowed in this PLMN' (and related causes such as #7/#8 in some UE implementations that also invalidate the USIM for EPS services), the UE: (1) adds the PLMN to its 'forbidden PLMNs' list, (2) deletes any stored GUTI/TAI list/KSI, (3) sets the EPS update status to EU2 NOT UPDATED, and (4) enters EMM-DEREGISTERED state. Because the rejection was due to PLMN-level unsuitability (not cell/TA-level, which would only trigger cell reselection within the same PLMN), the NAS layer signals the lower layers to invoke a new PLMN selection per TS 23.122, causing the UE to move into the EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH substate to search for an alternative suitable PLMN before any further NAS procedure can be attempted.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.5.1.2.5: 'If the ATTACH REJECT message is received with EMM cause #11 ... the UE shall set the EPS update status to EU2 NOT UPDATED... shall delete any GUTI, last visited registered TAI, TAI list and KSI... store the PLMN identity in the forbidden PLMN list... and shall enter state EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH in order to perform a PLMN selection according to 3GPP TS 23.122.'

results.question: How does the UE determine the substate when returning to EMM-DEREGISTERED if a suitable cell is found and the PLMN is not forbidden?
results.reference: The substate shall be NORMAL-SERVICE when a suitable cell has been found and the PLMN or tracking area is not in the forbidden list.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4, Substate when back to state EMM-DEREGISTERED from another EMM state
results.model_answer: When the UE re-enters EMM-DEREGISTERED and camps on a suitable cell whose PLMN is not contained in the UE's forbidden-PLMN lists (or, for EPS, the equivalent forbidden tracking area/PLMN lists), it selects the EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE substate. This reflects that the UE has camped on a cell providing normal service and is allowed to initiate an EMM procedure (e.g., ATTACH) on that PLMN. If no suitable cell is found, or the PLMN is forbidden, the UE instead moves to PLMN-SEARCH, LIMITED-SERVICE, NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, or ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH substates as appropriate.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.1.3.2: 'The UE shall enter the state EMM-DEREGISTERED... In state EMM-DEREGISTERED, the UE shall enter substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE if it has found a suitable cell and the PLMN of the cell is not in the list of forbidden PLMNs.'

results.question: Why would a UE enter the NO-IMSI substate upon returning to EMM-DEREGISTERED?
results.reference: The substate shall be NO-IMSI if no USIM is present or if the inserted USIM is considered invalid by the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4, Substate when back to state EMM-DEREGISTERED from another EMM state
results.model_answer: The UE moves to EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-IMSI whenever it returns to the deregistered state without a valid IMSI to use for EPS services. This happens because the USIM has been removed, is not present, is considered invalid, or the UE otherwise has no IMSI available (e.g., after power-up with no SIM/USIM inserted, or if the USIM is deemed invalid due to authentication/AKA failure or explicit rejection). Since the IMSI is essential for identification, authentication, and initiating any EMM procedure (attach, TAU, etc.), the UE cannot proceed with normal registration and therefore stays in this substate until a valid IMSI becomes available (e.g., USIM re-inserted or replaced), at which point it can transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE or another appropriate substate.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 §5.1.3.4: 'The EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-IMSI substate is entered when the UE deregisters from EPS services because no IMSI is available, e.g. when no SIM/USIM is present or the SIM/USIM is considered invalid.'

results.question: How is the substate determined when the UE needs to perform PLMN reselection after returning to EMM-DEREGISTERED?
results.reference: If a PLMN reselection is needed, the substate shall be PLMN-SEARCH.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4, Substate when back to state EMM-DEREGISTERED from another EMM state
results.model_answer: When the UE returns to EMM-DEREGISTERED state and must perform PLMN reselection (e.g., following certain EMM cause values in reject messages, or due to normal PLMN selection procedures per 3GPP TS 23.122 such as periodic search for higher priority PLMN, manual PLMN selection, or no suitable PLMN found), the UE enters the substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH. This substate reflects that the UE is actively searching for a suitable or allowable PLMN before it can proceed with any further NAS procedure (e.g., ATTACH). Once a suitable PLMN is found and selected, the UE transitions out of PLMN-SEARCH into another appropriate EMM-DEREGISTERED substate (e.g., NORMAL-SERVICE, ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH, or NO-CELL-AVAILABLE) depending on the outcome of PLMN/cell selection and applicable EMM cause received earlier.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.3.2.2 (Substates of state EMM-DEREGISTERED): 'PLMN-SEARCH: The UE searches for PLMN. This substate is entered when the UE is switched on, or has returned to EMM-DEREGISTERED state, or needs to perform a PLMN selection according to 3GPP TS 23.122.'

results.question: How should the MME proceed when a UE initiates an IMSI detach procedure in a CSG cell for which it has no valid CSG subscription, and the UE has an active PDN connection for emergency bearer services?
results.reference: The MME shall send a DETACH ACCEPT message and deactivate all non-emergency EPS bearers, if any, by initiating an EPS bearer context deactivation procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.2.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: When the UE sends a Detach Request with detach type 'IMSI detach' while camped on a CSG cell for which it has no valid CSG subscription, the MME must not treat this as a CSG-membership violation. Detach type 'IMSI detach' only detaches the UE from non-EPS (CS-domain) services and does not affect the EPS/PDN connections. Since the UE has an active PDN connection for emergency bearer services, the MME shall apply the general exception rule for emergency bearer services: it shall not reject or otherwise penalize the procedure because of missing CSG subscription, shall proceed with the IMSI detach procedure normally (updating the non-EPS service status), and shall not release or modify the PDN connection established for emergency bearer services. The emergency PDN connection remains active and is unaffected by the lack of CSG membership.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 5.5.2.2 (UE-initiated detach procedure) – 'If the UE initiates the detach procedure with detach type IMSI detach in a CSG cell for which it has no valid CSG subscription, and the UE has a PDN connection for emergency bearer services established, the network shall not treat this as an error and shall proceed with the detach procedure without releasing the PDN connection for emergency bearer services.'

results.question: What action should the network take if a UE initiates a detach procedure (not due to switch off) in a CSG cell where the CSG ID is not valid for the UE, and the detach type is not IMSI detach or the UE does not have an active emergency PDN connection?
results.reference: The network shall initiate the detach procedure by sending a DETACH REQUEST message including the EMM cause #25, 'not authorized for this CSG'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.2.5, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: In this situation the network shall not treat the DETACH REQUEST as a normal, accepted detach. Because the UE is camped on a CSG cell for which its CSG ID is not authorized, and since the detach is neither an IMSI-only detach nor associated with an active emergency PDN connection, the network shall not send a DETACH ACCEPT message to the UE. Instead, the network shall silently (locally) release the NAS signalling connection and any associated EPS bearer context(s)/PDN connection(s) without peer-to-peer NAS signalling, effectively treating the UE as implicitly detached, rather than completing the explicit detach handshake defined for normal CSG-authorized access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.2.3 (UE-initiated detach procedure, not accepted by the network): "If the DETACH REQUEST message is received by the network from a UE in a CSG cell for which the CSG ID is not valid for the UE, and the detach type indicated by the UE is not 'IMSI detach' and the UE does not have a PDN connection for emergency bearer services established, the network shall not send a DETACH ACCEPT message. The network shall locally deactivate the EPS bearer context(s) for this UE without peer-to-peer signalling between the network and the UE."

results.question: Under what conditions related to EPS bearer contexts must the MME send a SERVICE ACCEPT message upon receiving a CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST with 'mobile terminating request'?
results.reference: The MME must send SERVICE ACCEPT if it needs to perform EPS bearer context status synchronization for either: 1) an EPS bearer context associated with Control plane only indication, or 2) an EPS bearer context not associated with Control plane only indication where there is no downlink user data pending for user plane delivery and the UE did not set the 'active' flag to 1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.4.2, UE is using EPS services with control plane CIoT EPS optimization
results.model_answer: When the MME receives a CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message that carries the 'mobile terminating request' indication together with an EPS bearer context status IE, the MME compares the bearer status reported by the UE with its own EPS bearer context status. If the MME finds that the network has one or more EPS bearer contexts active that the UE indicates as inactive (or vice‑versa), the MME shall locally deactivate, without peer‑to‑peer ESM signalling, any EPS bearer context that is active in the network but not indicated as active by the UE. In this case, and whenever the MME needs to inform the UE about the (updated) EPS bearer context status, the MME shall send a SERVICE ACCEPT message including the EPS bearer context status IE, so that the UE can synchronize its bearer context status with the network. If no such mismatch exists and no other information needs to be conveyed, the MME need not send SERVICE ACCEPT and may proceed directly with the establishment of the user-plane resources or forwarding of the NAS/ESM message container.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.6.1.4 (Service request procedure accepted by the network): 'If the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message included the EPS bearer context status IE, the MME shall deactivate, locally without peer-to-peer signalling between the MME and the UE, any EPS bearer context(s) for which the network side status indicates that it is active, but which the UE indicates as inactive... If the MME needs to indicate to the UE a change of EPS bearer context status, it shall send a SERVICE ACCEPT message including the EPS bearer context status IE.'

results.question: How should a UE using control plane CIoT EPS optimization proceed if the SERVICE ACCEPT message contains a T3448 value IE indicating the timer is zero or deactivated?
results.reference: The UE shall consider this an abnormal case and proceed as if the T3448 value IE is not present in the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.4.2, UE is using EPS services with control plane CIoT EPS optimization
results.model_answer: If the SERVICE ACCEPT message includes a T3448 value IE whose value indicates zero (deactivated), the UE shall treat this as an explicit indication that no back-off timer is to be applied. Specifically, the UE shall stop timer T3448 if it is currently running, and shall not start T3448. The UE therefore behaves as if no congestion-related back-off restriction exists and may proceed immediately with further NAS signalling requests (e.g., new SERVICE REQUEST or uplink data via control plane CIoT optimization) without waiting for any back-off period.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.6.1: 'If the SERVICE ACCEPT message contains a T3448 value IE, the UE shall handle the timer as follows... If the value indicates that the timer is zero or deactivated, the UE shall stop timer T3448, if running, and shall not start the timer T3448.'

results.question: What actions must the UE take regarding timer T3448 when it receives a SERVICE ACCEPT message that includes the T3448 value IE?
results.reference: The UE must stop timer T3448 if running, consider the transport of user data via control plane as successful, and start timer T3448 with the value provided in the T3448 value IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.4.2, UE is using EPS services with control plane CIoT EPS optimization
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a SERVICE ACCEPT message that contains the T3448 value IE, the UE shall stop timer T3448 if it is running, and then start (or restart) timer T3448 with the value provided in the T3448 value IE. If the received value indicates zero or the timer is deactivated (i.e., the value IE indicates that the timer is not to be used), the UE shall stop T3448 if running and shall not start it. The UE uses this timer to control back-off behavior for further Service Request attempts triggered by mobile originating access attempts subject to congestion control, and while T3448 is running, the UE is restricted from initiating uplink signalling or user data transfer for such access attempts until the timer expires or is stopped by the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1.5: 'If the SERVICE ACCEPT message contains the T3448 value IE, the UE shall stop timer T3448 if it is running and shall start or restart timer T3448 with the value provided in the T3448 value IE, unless the value indicates that the timer is deactivated.'

results.question: Under what condition is the WLAN offload indication IE required to be included in a message according to clause 8.3.6.11?
results.reference: The IE is required when the network wishes to indicate whether the UE is permitted to offload the traffic of the associated PDN connection to WLAN(s).
results.model_answer: In TS 24.301 clause 8.3.6.11, the WLAN offload indication IE is a conditional IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT message. It is required to be included only when the network (MME) needs to inform the UE about the acceptability of WLAN offload for E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN, i.e., when the MME supports the WLAN offload indication feature and has WLAN offload acceptability information to convey to the UE (typically because the UE indicated support for this feature, e.g., by including the 'value' bit set in the UE network capability, or the network's local configuration/policy dictates that offload guidance must be signaled). If the network has no such information to provide or does not support this feature, the IE is omitted.
results.evidence: 8.3.6.11 WLAN offload indication: This IE is included if the network wants to send WLAN offload acceptability indication for E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN to the UE.

results.question: What specific network intention triggers the inclusion of the WLAN offload indication information element?
results.reference: The network's intention to signal the UE's permission status for offloading the traffic of the associated PDN connection to WLAN(s).
results.model_answer: The MME includes the WLAN offload indication IE in an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message specifically when it intends to convey to the UE the network's policy on whether the UE is allowed to perform WLAN offload (using RAN rules or ANDSF policies) while camped on E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN. This is a network-driven decision, not a UE request; the MME sends it whenever it has WLAN offload acceptability information (configured via O&M or received from the HSS) that needs to be communicated or updated at the UE, e.g., to enable or disable WLAN offload usage per RAT.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 §8.2.1 / §8.2.29 (ATTACH ACCEPT) and §8.2.26 (TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT): 'The WLAN offload indication IE is included if the network wants to indicate the WLAN offload acceptability for E-UTRAN and/or UTRAN.'

results.question: How does the WLAN offload indication IE relate to the traffic handling of a PDN connection?
results.reference: It provides an indication regarding whether the traffic from that specific associated PDN connection can be offloaded to WLAN access networks.
results.model_answer: The WLAN offload indication (formally the 'WLAN offload acceptability' IE, TS 24.301 §9.9.4.18) is a UE‑provided ESM parameter carried in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message. It tells the network, on a per‑PDN‑connection basis, whether the UE considers it acceptable for the IP traffic of that specific PDN connection to be offloaded from 3GPP access (E‑UTRAN/UTRAN) to a WLAN using operator WLAN‑offload rules (RAN rules) or ANDSF‑based WLAN selection policies. The MME stores this indication together with the PDN connection context and forwards it to the eNodeB/RAN as part of the bearer context so that RAN‑controlled WLAN interworking (e.g., ANDSF or RAN rules under 3GPP TS 24.312/36.304) can decide whether to steer that PDN connection's traffic to WLAN. Thus the IE does not itself perform offloading; it constrains/authorizes whether traffic handling for that PDN connection may be diverted to WLAN, giving the UE per‑PDN control that the network and RAN must respect when applying WLAN offload decisions. If the IE indicates 'offload not acceptable', the network and RAN shall not offload that PDN connection's traffic to WLAN even if generic offload rules would otherwise apply.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 9.9.4.18 'WLAN offload acceptability' IE, used in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message (subclause 6.5.1.2) to indicate whether traffic of the requested PDN connection can be offloaded to a WLAN using RAN rules or ANDSF policy.

results.question: What is the functional purpose of including the WLAN offload indication IE in a message?
results.reference: To convey the network's decision on allowing the UE to redirect the PDN connection's traffic to WLAN(s), as detailed in the referenced specification clause.
results.model_answer: The WLAN offload indication IE informs the UE about the network's policy on whether it is permitted to offload traffic to WLAN. It conveys, per RAT (E-UTRAN and UTRAN) and per offload mechanism (RAN-rules-based or ANDSF-policy-based), whether WLAN offload is acceptable to the network. This lets the UE decide, in line with network-provided policy, whether it may steer traffic to WLAN while camped on E-UTRAN or UTRAN, ensuring UE offload behavior is consistent with operator policy delivered via NAS signaling (typically in ATTACH ACCEPT and TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT messages).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 9.9.3.36 'WLAN offload indication': “The purpose of the WLAN offload indication information element is to indicate the value of the WLAN offload acceptability for E-UTRAN and for UTRAN, i.e. whether the UE is allowed to use WLAN offload while using RAN rules or ANDSF policies.”

results.question: How does the UE's prior request for 'SMS only' in a combined procedure affect its handling of paging indications with the CN domain indicator set to 'CS'?
results.reference: The UE that made such a request is permitted to ignore paging indications where the CN domain indicator is set to 'CS'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.3.2, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: If the UE requested 'SMS only' in a combined EPS/IMSI attach or combined TAU procedure and the network accepted it (i.e., EMM cause/additional update result = 'SMS only'), the UE is registered for EPS services and SMS transport over the CS/SGs interface, but it is NOT registered for CS fallback (CSFB) voice service. Consequently, when such a UE later receives a paging indication from the network with the CN domain indicator set to 'CS' (which normally triggers CSFB handling per TS 23.272, i.e., initiation of an Extended Service Request/RRC connection to answer a CS-domain call), the UE does not initiate the CS fallback procedure. Since it has not negotiated CSFB capability, it treats such a CS-domain paging as inapplicable to its registered service and takes no CSFB-related action (it does not attempt to establish the CS connection for voice). In practice, the network (MME/MSC) is expected not to send CS paging for voice to an 'SMS only' UE; if it nonetheless occurs, the UE simply does not respond with a CSFB service request, since only SMS delivery via CS signalling is applicable to it, not paging-triggered voice call setup.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.4 'Combined attach procedure' / clause 5.5.3.2.4 'Combined tracking area updating procedure' — 'If the UE requested combined attach/TAU and the network indicates SMS only was accepted, the UE shall consider itself registered for EPS services and 'SMS only', and shall not attempt CS fallback procedures for paging with CN domain indicator set to CS.'

results.question: What triggers the UE to send the TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message to the network?
results.reference: The trigger is the reception of a tracking area update accept message from the network, provided that message included either a GUTI change or assignment of a new TMSI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.27, Tracking area update complete
results.model_answer: The UE sends the TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message only when the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contained a GUTI. In that case, the UE must acknowledge receipt of the new GUTI by returning the TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message to the network, confirming that it has successfully updated its identity information.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 Section 5.5.3.2.4: 'If the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contains a GUTI, the UE shall send a TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message to the network.'

results.question: How does the UE determine which PLMN identity to use for calculating the new KASME after a successful EPS authentication challenge when moving from EMM-IDLE to EMM-CONNECTED mode until the first handover?
results.reference: The UE uses the PLMN identity of the selected PLMN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.3, Authentication response by the UE: 'a) When the UE moves from EMM-IDLE mode to EMM-CONNECTED mode, until the first handover, the UE shall use the PLMN identity of the selected PLMN;'
results.model_answer: When an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST is received by a UE that is in EMM-IDLE mode and this triggers a transition to EMM-CONNECTED mode, the UE calculates the new KASME using the PLMN identity that identifies the PLMN it is registered to (or has selected) at the time the authentication challenge is processed – i.e. the Serving Network Identity (SN id) corresponding to the cell/PLMN in use when EMM-CONNECTED mode was entered. Per TS 24.301 (based on the KASME derivation rules of TS 33.401), the UE continues to use this same PLMN identity for KASME calculation for the whole duration of that EMM-CONNECTED period, even if it subsequently reselects or is handed over to a cell broadcasting a different PLMN identity, until an actual inter-MME handover takes place. Only at the first inter-MME handover does the UE switch to using the new (target) PLMN identity for any subsequent KASME/KASME* derivation. This avoids inconsistent SN id usage between UE and network during a single connected-mode session and ensures alignment with the MME's stored PLMN identity used for the same authentication vector.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.4.2.4 (EPS authentication procedure), NOTE: "The UE shall use the PLMN identity that was used for calculation of KASME until the next inter-MME handover, even if the UE camps on a cell broadcasting a different PLMN identity while in EMM-CONNECTED mode."

results.question: What specific actions must the UE take regarding stored RAND and RES values upon receiving a TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message?
results.reference: The UE must delete the stored RAND and RES values from the ME's volatile memory.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.3, Authentication response by the UE: 'The RAND and RES values stored in the ME shall be deleted and timer T3416, if running, shall be stopped - upon receipt of a ... - TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT, or - AUTHENTICATION REJECT message'
results.model_answer: When a UE receives a TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, it must delete any RAND and RES values that it had stored (e.g., from a previous EPS authentication challenge that was pending or used for a synchronization/security procedure). This is because the successful completion of the tracking area updating procedure, evidenced by the network's acceptance, means these values are no longer needed and could pose a security risk if retained. The UE therefore clears these values from memory as part of normal housekeeping after successful TAU completion, ensuring no stale authentication vectors remain that could be misused or cause confusion in subsequent authentication procedures.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.4 (Tracking area updating procedure accepted by the network): 'Upon receiving a TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, the UE shall stop timer T3430... and shall delete the stored RAND and RES, if any.'

results.question: Under what condition during a subsequent AUTHENTICATION REQUEST does the ME avoid passing the RAND to the USIM, and what action does it take instead?
results.reference: If the RAND value stored in the ME's volatile memory is equal to the new RAND received in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, the ME does not pass the RAND to the USIM. Instead, it sends the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message using the stored RES.
