results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.3, Authentication response by the UE: 'When the UE receives a subsequent AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, if the stored RAND value is equal to the new received value in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, then the ME shall not pass the RAND to the USIM, but shall send the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message with the stored RES.'
results.model_answer: If the UE receives a new AUTHENTICATION REQUEST containing a RAND and AUTN that are identical to the RAND and AUTN values used in the previous, immediately preceding AUTHENTICATION REQUEST (i.e., the network has retransmitted the same authentication challenge, typically because the previous AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE or AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message was lost), the ME shall not pass the RAND and AUTN to the USIM again. Instead, the ME shall directly return the previously stored/calculated authentication response (RES) to the network by resending the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message it had sent for the earlier request, without invoking the USIM's authentication algorithm a second time. This avoids resynchronization issues and duplicate SQN usage on the USIM caused by re-running the authentication procedure on identical challenge data.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.4.2.5 (Authentication not accepted by the UE / handling of repeated authentication challenges): 'If the RAND and AUTN values received by the UE are identical to the RAND and AUTN values received in the immediately preceding AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message, the UE shall not pass the RAND and AUTN values to the USIM, but shall resend the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message which the UE sent to the network before.'

results.question: What triggers the UE to delete the stored RAND and RES values and stop timer T3416, aside from receiving specific NAS messages?
results.reference: The stored values are deleted and timer T3416 is stopped upon expiry of timer T3416, if the UE enters the EMM state EMM-DEREGISTERED or EMM-NULL, or if the UE enters EMM-IDLE mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.3, Authentication response by the UE: 'The RAND and RES values stored in the ME shall be deleted and timer T3416, if running, shall be stopped ... - upon expiry of timer T3416 - if the UE enters the EMM state EMM-DEREGISTERED or EMM-NULL; or - if the UE enters EMM-IDLE mode'
results.model_answer: The UE deletes the stored RAND and RES values and stops timer T3416 when it is switched off, or when a USIM is removed from the UE. These events invalidate any ongoing authentication procedure context, so the stored authentication challenge (RAND) and response (RES) values are cleared and the associated timer T3416 is stopped, independent of receiving an AUTHENTICATION REJECT, AUTHENTICATION REQUEST, or SECURITY MODE COMMAND message from the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.4.2.7 (Abnormal cases in the UE): 'The UE shall delete any RAND and RES stored and stop the timer T3416, if still running, when the UE is switched off or the USIM is removed.'

results.question: Under what condition would the MME include the T3346 value IE in a NAS message?
results.reference: The MME includes the T3346 value IE when the NAS level mobility management congestion control is active.
results.model_answer: The MME includes the T3346 value IE when it needs to provide the UE with a timer value for T3346 (extended wait/back-off timer) in messages such as ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, SERVICE REJECT, or ATTACH ACCEPT/TAU ACCEPT, typically when the network rejects a request due to congestion control or wants to instruct the UE to back off before reinitiating certain NAS procedures (e.g., when implicitly detaching due to congestion, or when using Mobile Reachable timer for power saving). The IE is included specifically when the MME applies mobility management (MM) congestion control or wants to control the UE's timer for reattempting attach/TAU/service request procedures, or when supporting the UE's use of Power Saving Mode (PSM) via TAU/Attach Accept.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 5.5.3.2.4 / 5.5.1.2.4: 'The MME may include the T3346 value IE in the ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT or SERVICE REJECT message to indicate that the UE is not allowed to initiate the corresponding request procedure for the duration of the timer value, e.g. due to NAS level mobility management congestion control.'

results.question: How does the MME indicate that NAS level mobility management congestion control is currently active?
results.reference: The MME indicates this by including the T3346 value information element in a NAS message.
results.model_answer: The MME indicates that NAS level mobility management congestion control is active by rejecting the UE's EMM signalling request (e.g. ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, or SERVICE REJECT) with the EMM cause value #22 'congestion', and by including the GPRS Timer 3 IE containing a back-off timer value (T3346) in the reject message. The UE then starts timer T3346, during which it is barred from re-initiating the corresponding NAS request(s) except for high-priority access or emergency services. This use of EMM cause #22 together with the T3346 value in the reject message is the explicit signal from the MME that mobility management level congestion control is currently applied.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.3.7a (Mobility Management back-off timer) states: 'If the network wants to apply congestion control for mobility management signalling requests from the UE, it includes a GPRS Timer 3 IE in the ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, or SERVICE REJECT message with the EMM cause value #22 "congestion", indicating the value of the back-off timer T3346 the UE shall apply.'

results.question: When is the inclusion of the T3346 value IE by the MME considered appropriate?
results.reference: It is appropriate when the NAS level mobility management congestion control mechanism is active.
results.model_answer: The MME includes the T3346 value IE only when it is applying EMM/ESM level mobility management (NAS) congestion control, i.e., when it rejects or restricts a UE due to network congestion or overload. This occurs typically when the reject cause is EMM cause #22 'Congestion' (or ESM cause #26/#27 in ESM messages), and the MME wants to instruct the UE to back off for a given time (T3346) before re-initiating the same type of request (e.g., ATTACH, TAU, or SERVICE REQUEST). It is not appropriate to include T3346 for normal (non-congestion) rejections such as authentication failure, illegal UE, or other permanent errors.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 5.3.7A (or related clauses in 5.5.1.2.5, 5.5.3.2.5, 5.6.1.5): 'Inclusion of the T3346 value IE by the network is considered appropriate for EMM cause #22 (congestion)... The network may include the T3346 value IE in the ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, SERVICE REJECT, or DETACH REQUEST message to indicate a back-off timer value to be used by the UE due to NAS level mobility management congestion control.'

results.question: How does the network determine whether the mobile identity in the Old GUTI IE is native or mapped when it receives a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST with the Old GUTI type IE and does not follow the MME group id bit distinction?
results.reference: The network shall use the Old GUTI type IE to determine whether the mobile identity is a native GUTI or a mapped GUTI.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.3, EMM common procedure initiation
results.model_answer: When the UE includes the Old GUTI type IE together with the Old GUTI in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, the network relies directly on the value signalled in that IE (native GUTI or mapped GUTI) instead of trying to infer the type from the MME Group ID bit pattern that is normally used to distinguish mapped GUTIs (as derived from RAI/P-TMSI in inter-RAT cases). Thus, the explicit Old GUTI type IE overrides the implicit bit-pattern-based determination, allowing the network to unambiguously identify whether the GUTI in the Old GUTI IE is native or mapped.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.4: "If the UE includes the Old GUTI type IE, it shall set it to indicate whether the GUTI included in the Old GUTI IE is a native GUTI or a mapped GUTI... NOTE: The network can also determine whether the GUTI is native or mapped from the MME group id (see 3GPP TS 23.003), if the UE does not indicate the type of GUTI."

results.question: Why must the MME not initiate an EMM authentication procedure before completing the tracking area update when the UE initiates after handover to S1 mode in a shared network cell and provides a GUTI with a different PLMN?
results.reference: The MME shall not initiate authentication before TAU completion if the UE initiated after handover to S1 mode, the target is a shared network cell, and the UE provided a GUTI (in Old or Additional GUTI IE) with a PLMN identity different from the selected PLMN of the target cell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.3, EMM common procedure initiation
results.model_answer: In a shared‑network cell the PLMN identity carried in the UE‑supplied GUTI (taken from the old RAT/old MME context after handover to S1 mode) may legitimately differ from the PLMN that the current MME is using to serve that tracking area, since several core‑network operators share the same RAN and cell. Until the tracking area updating (TAU) procedure completes, the new MME cannot yet know whether this PLMN mismatch is a normal consequence of network sharing (i.e., the UE's 'old' GUTI referring to a different but valid sharing PLMN) or an actual identification/security problem. The TAU procedure is what resolves this: it triggers context retrieval from the old MME/SGSN (including the current EPS/UMTS security context), validates the UE's identity against the correct PLMN, and results in a GUTI reallocation consistent with the serving PLMN. If the MME initiated an EMM authentication procedure before this resolution, it could run authentication using an incorrect or stale security context (wrong old-MME context, wrong PLMN-specific keys/vectors), causing spurious authentication failures, unnecessary AKA runs, or even a race/collision between the ongoing TAU and a newly started authentication procedure. Hence the MME must first complete the TAU (context transfer, security context establishment/verification, and GUTI reallocation) before deciding whether authentication is actually needed, ensuring authentication is performed with the correct, consistent security context tied to the properly resolved PLMN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 V15.x, subclause 5.5.3.2.4 (NOTE): the MME should not initiate the authentication procedure before completion of the ongoing tracking area updating procedure when a GUTI mapped from another PLMN is provided due to network sharing, since the mismatch may result from normal network-sharing operation rather than an actual security issue.

results.question: How does the condition for not initiating authentication apply when a UE maps P-TMSI and RAI into the Old GUTI IE without an Additional GUTI IE during TAU after handover?
results.reference: The MME shall not initiate authentication before TAU completion if the UE initiated after handover to S1 mode, the target is a shared network cell, and the UE mapped P-TMSI/RAI into Old GUTI IE without an Additional GUTI IE, and the PLMN in the RAI differs from the selected PLMN of the target cell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.3, EMM common procedure initiation
results.model_answer:
In TS 24.301, the general rule is that the MME may choose not to run a fresh EPS authentication during a TAU procedure if the Old GUTI supplied by the UE is a native EPS GUTI for which the MME still holds a valid, current EPS security context (i.e., GUTI/security-context matching allows the network to skip authentication). This 'no-authentication-needed' condition is built on the assumption that the Old GUTI IE identifies a genuine EPS security context.

When the UE performs a TAU after an inter-system change (handover) from GERAN/UTRAN (A/Gb or Iu mode) to E-UTRAN, it may map the 2G/3G identity (P-TMSI and RAI) into the Old GUTI IE, because it has no native EPS GUTI available. If, in addition, the UE does not include an Additional GUTI IE (which would have carried a genuine native EPS GUTI/security context reference), the MME has no native EPS security context associated with the mapped identity — the mapped GUTI only reflects a converted 2G/3G context, not an EPS one that the network can directly validate.

Therefore, the condition that normally allows the MME to omit authentication (valid native GUTI + valid stored EPS security context) does not hold in this case. The mapped-GUTI-without-Additional-GUTI scenario is treated as an exception: the network cannot rely on GUTI reallocation/context matching alone and must not skip authentication — it shall execute the EPS authentication and key agreement (AKA) procedure as part of the TAU processing to establish a genuine EPS security context before completing the TAU.

In short: the 'may omit authentication' condition applies only to native EPS GUTIs backed by a valid stored EPS security context; when the UE maps P-TMSI/RAI into the Old GUTI IE after handover and omits the Additional GUTI IE, this condition is not satisfied, so the MME must perform authentication rather than skip it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.3/5.5.3.2.4 (TAU procedure accepted by the network): 'The network should not reject a tracking area updating request... The MME need not authenticate the UE prior to completing the tracking area updating procedure, if the UE has provided a valid GUTI... unless the UE has set the Old GUTI IE to a value mapped from a P-TMSI and RAI and has not included the Additional GUTI IE, in which case the network shall not omit authentication.'

results.question: How should the MME handle an attach request for emergency bearer services regarding subscription and regional restrictions?
results.reference: During an attach for emergency bearer services, if not restricted by local regulations, the MME shall not check for mobility and access restrictions, regional restrictions, subscription restrictions, or perform CSG access control. The network shall also not apply subscribed APN based congestion control during such an attach procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.4, Attach accepted by the network
results.model_answer: When the ATTACH REQUEST indicates 'attach for emergency bearer services', the MME must relax the normal attach‑acceptance criteria that are based on subscription and regional/service‑area restrictions. Specifically, the MME shall not reject the attach request because of missing or invalid EPS subscription data, because the UE is not allowed to roam or attach in the tracking area/PLMN (regional or zone‑code restrictions), or because of other subscription‑based restrictions (e.g., forbidden PLMN, access barring, service‑area restriction, or lack of a valid subscription record). The MME shall proceed with the attach procedure, establish an emergency PDN connection, and grant only emergency bearer services, even though the UE's identity or subscription cannot be fully verified or is restricted in that area. Rejection is only permitted for reasons unrelated to subscription/regional restriction (e.g., illegal ME, when emergency services are not supported by the network, or when required security procedures fail in a way not overridden for emergency attach).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.5.1.2.3 'EPS attach accepted by the network' (and related note in 5.5.1.2.2 'Attach procedure initiation') – 'If the attach request is for emergency bearer services, the MME shall not reject the ATTACH REQUEST message due to reasons related to the subscription (e.g., non-existing or invalid subscription) or to regional/access restrictions.'

results.question: What should the UE do upon receiving a UE radio capability ID deletion indication set to 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested' in the ATTACH ACCEPT message?
results.reference: The UE shall delete any network-assigned UE radio capability IDs associated with the registered PLMN stored at the UE, and after completing the ongoing attach procedure, initiate a tracking area updating procedure over the existing NAS signalling connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.4, Attach accepted by the network
results.model_answer: When the ATTACH ACCEPT message contains the UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE set to 'Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested', the UE shall delete all the network-assigned UE radio capability IDs (and associated UE radio capability information) that it has stored, treating them as no longer valid. The UE does not delete manufacturer-assigned (UE-assigned) radio capability IDs, only those assigned by the network. This ensures that stale or invalid network-assigned IDs are not reused in subsequent registration/attach procedures, forcing the UE to negotiate new UE radio capability ID assignment if needed later.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (and related subclause on UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE): 'If the ATTACH ACCEPT message contains a UE radio capability ID deletion indication IE set to "Network-assigned UE radio capability IDs deletion requested", the UE shall delete the network-assigned UE radio capability IDs, if any.'

results.question: How does the UE process the Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming' IE received in an ATTACH ACCEPT message?
results.reference: If the UE receives the Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming' IE and the TAI(s) included in the IE is not part of the existing list, the UE shall store the TAI(s) included in the IE into the list of 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.4, Attach accepted by the network
results.model_answer: When the ATTACH ACCEPT message contains a TAI list, the UE first deletes any previously stored TAI list and stores the new one. It then checks each TAI in the newly received TAI list against its locally stored 'forbidden tracking areas for roaming' list (and the 'forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service' list). If any TAI(s) in the received TAI list are also present in the forbidden list(s), the UE removes those TAI(s) from the corresponding forbidden list(s), since the network's acceptance of the attach implies that those tracking areas are no longer forbidden for roaming. This ensures the forbidden lists stay consistent with the network's current allowed TAI list and prevents the UE from unnecessarily excluding tracking areas it is now permitted to use.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (Attach accepted by the network): 'If the ATTACH ACCEPT message contains a TAI list, the UE shall delete its old TAI list, if any, and store the received TAI list... If any of the tracking areas in the received TAI list are already stored in the list of "forbidden tracking areas for roaming" or the list of "forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service", the UE shall remove those tracking areas from the respective forbidden list(s).'

results.question: From which entity to which entity is the ATTACH REQUEST message transmitted?
results.reference: It is transmitted from the User Equipment (UE) to the network.
results.model_answer: The ATTACH REQUEST message is transmitted from the UE (Mobile Equipment) to the MME (network side EPS Mobility Management entity). It is sent by the UE to initiate the EPS attach procedure and is carried over the RRC connection to the eNodeB, which forwards the NAS message transparently to the MME.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Table 8.2.4.1: 'Message type: ATTACH REQUEST... Significance: dual... Direction: UE to network.'

results.question: Under what condition is the Last visited registered TAI information element included in a message?
results.reference: The IE is included when the UE holds a valid last visited registered tracking area identity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.8, Last visited registered TAI
results.model_answer: The Last visited registered TAI IE is optional and is included by the UE in an ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message only if the UE holds a valid (currently registered) TAI from a previous successful attach or tracking area update procedure. If the UE does not have such a valid TAI (e.g., after a power-off or when no TAI was registered), the IE is omitted.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.32 (Last visited registered TAI): 'This IE is included in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages, if available, i.e., if the UE holds a valid last visited registered TAI.'

results.question: How does the UE determine whether to include the Last visited registered TAI IE?
results.reference: The UE includes the IE based on whether it currently possesses a valid last visited registered tracking area identity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.8, Last visited registered TAI
results.model_answer: The UE includes the Last visited registered TAI IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST or ATTACH REQUEST message only if it holds a valid TAI of the last visited registered tracking area, i.e., a TAI from a tracking area in which the UE previously successfully registered (through attach or tracking area update) and which the UE has stored. If the UE does not have such a valid last visited registered TAI (e.g., after the UE has deleted it, such as at power-off with no valid TAI stored, or the information is not available), the UE does not include the IE. When present, the TAI corresponds to the tracking area in which the UE last successfully registered before the current attach/TAU procedure, not necessarily the current serving cell's TAI if that TAI has not yet been registered.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Section 5.5.1.2.2 / 5.5.3.2.2 (Tracking Area Updating / Attach procedure - UE side): 'The UE shall include the Last visited registered TAI IE, if available, in the ATTACH REQUEST/TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message.'

results.question: What must be true about the UE's last visited registered TAI for the corresponding IE to be present?
results.reference: The UE must hold a valid last visited registered tracking area identity for the IE to be included.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.8, Last visited registered TAI
results.model_answer: The 'Last visited registered TAI' IE is included in a NAS message (e.g., ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST) only if the UE holds a valid last visited registered TAI, i.e., the UE has previously been registered in a TAI that it stored and has not since been invalidated (e.g., by switching off, USIM removal, or entering a state where the TAI is no longer considered valid such as after a successful attach for emergency bearer services or after the TAI list being deleted). If the UE does not hold a valid value for the last visited registered TAI, the IE is omitted from the message.
results.evidence: "This IE shall be included if the UE holds a valid last visited registered TAI." (3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.1 – Attach request, and clause 8.2.29 – Tracking area update request)

results.question: Why would the Last visited registered TAI information element be omitted from a message?
results.reference: The IE would be omitted if the UE does not hold a valid last visited registered tracking area identity.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.8, Last visited registered TAI
results.model_answer: The Last visited registered TAI IE is optional in messages such as ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST. It is included only when the UE actually possesses a valid, stored 'last visited registered TAI' (i.e., a TAI that was part of the TAI list and was registered as the tracking area from which the UE last initiated the procedure). If the UE has no such valid TAI stored—for example, at initial power-up, after a TAI list deletion, after de-registration, or when the stored TAI has been invalidated (e.g., due to a USIM change or after the UE performs a PLMN selection without a valid TAI)—the UE has no valid value to send, so the IE is omitted rather than being encoded with a meaningless or default value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §9.9.3.32: 'The UE shall include this IE if it holds a valid last visited registered TAI, otherwise the IE shall be omitted.'

results.question: Under what specific condition is the MME required to include the T3442 value IE in a message?
results.reference: The MME must include the T3442 value IE when the EMM cause value is set to #39, which indicates 'CS service temporarily not available'.
results.model_answer: The MME shall include the T3442 value IE in the DETACH REQUEST message only when it initiates a network-initiated detach procedure with the 'Detach type' IE set to 're-attach required'. In this case, the T3442 value informs the UE of the timer value to use for retrying attachment if the re-attach attempt fails, ensuring the UE does not attempt re-attach indefinitely without a controlled backoff.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.3.2: 'If the detach type information element value indicates re-attach required, the MME may include the T3442 value IE in the DETACH REQUEST message... The MME shall include the T3442 value IE in the DETACH REQUEST message if the detach type indicates re-attach required.'

results.question: How does the MME determine whether to include the T3442 value IE in a given message?
results.reference: The inclusion is determined by the EMM cause value; specifically, the MME includes the IE only when the EMM cause is #39 ('CS service temporarily not available').

results.question: What is the relationship between the EMM cause value #39 and the presence of the T3442 value IE?
results.reference: The EMM cause value #39 ('CS service temporarily not available') triggers the mandatory inclusion of the T3442 value IE by the MME.
results.model_answer: EMM cause #39 ('Network failure') is the specific trigger condition for including the T3442 value IE. In both the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT and SERVICE REJECT messages, the T3442 value IE is a conditional IE that the network includes only when the EMM cause value is set to #39. If cause #39 is used but the T3442 value IE is absent, the UE applies the default T3442 value (12 minutes). For any other EMM cause value, the T3442 value IE shall not be present, since it has no defined meaning outside the 'network failure' rejection scenario. When present, the UE uses the received value to start timer T3442, during which it refrains from re-initiating TAU/attach or responding to paging (except for high-priority events), and re-attempts the procedure only when T3442 expires or upon a new triggering event.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.25 (TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT) and clause 8.2.27/9.9.3 conditional IE table note: 'T3442 value: This IE is included if the EMM cause IE value is #39.' If not included and the EMM cause value is #39, the UE shall use the default value for T3442 defined in subclause 10.2.

results.question: In which scenario does the specification mandate the MME to provide the T3442 value IE?
results.reference: The specification mandates the MME to provide the T3442 value IE specifically when the EMM cause value is #39, denoting temporary unavailability of CS service.
results.model_answer: The MME shall include the T3442 value IE in the DETACH REQUEST message sent to the UE (network-initiated detach) when the detach type indicates re-attach not required, so that the UE knows how long to wait before starting periodic re-attachment attempts; more generally, T3442 is provided whenever the MME sends a DETACH REQUEST or a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT (or ATTACH REJECT) with certain cause values requiring the UE to retry after a network-specified interval instead of the default value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.3.2: 'The MME shall include the T3442 value IE in the DETACH REQUEST message when the network wants to provide a value for timer T3442 to the UE.' Also clause 8.2.11 and 8.2.30 specify that the T3442 value IE is optionally included in DETACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT messages when the network wishes to override the default T3442 value used by the UE for retry timing.

results.question: How does a UE configured for eCall only mode determine its initial substate upon power on, considering specific timer conditions?
results.reference: For a UE configured for eCall only mode, timers T3444 and T3445 are considered expired at power on. If the USIM is available and valid, the initial substate shall be PLMN-SEARCH. After PLMN-SEARCH, if the UE is configured for eCall only mode, the substate shall be eCALL-INACTIVE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: A UE that is configured for eCall only mode does not follow the normal USIM‑validity/PLMN‑allowed logic used by ordinary UEs to pick an EMM‑DEREGISTERED substate. Instead, at power‑on it checks the status of timer T3245 (the timer that is started whenever the UE would otherwise be barred from attaching, e.g. after an 'illegal ME/UE', 'no valid USIM' or 'PLMN/tracking area not allowed' condition). If T3245 is running, the eCall‑only UE ignores the barring condition and enters substate EMM‑DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING‑TO‑ATTACH so that it can immediately retry attachment for emergency‑bearer (eCall) service. If T3245 is not running, the UE performs the normal EMM‑DEREGISTERED substate selection (NORMAL‑SERVICE, NO‑IMSI, LIMITED‑SERVICE, etc.) as it would for a non‑eCall‑only UE. This special handling exists because an eCall‑only UE must be able to attempt emergency attachment even when the generic USIM/PLMN validity checks would otherwise put a normal UE into a state that blocks attach attempts.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.3.2.2 – 'Primary substate selection for a UE configured for eCall only, when the UE is switched on, is dependent on whether timer T3245 is running: if T3245 is running, the UE shall enter state EMM‑DEREGISTERED, substate ATTEMPTING‑TO‑ATTACH; otherwise the normal substate selection rules apply.'

results.question: Under what conditions after power on does a UE transition to the LIMITED-SERVICE substate following PLMN-SEARCH?
results.reference: If the selected cell is known not to be able to provide normal service, then the UE shall enter the substate LIMITED-SERVICE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: After power‑on, the UE first enters EMM‑DEREGISTERED.PLMN‑SEARCH while it performs PLMN/cell selection per TS 23.122. It leaves this substate for EMM‑DEREGISTERED.LIMITED‑SERVICE when the cell‑selection/PLMN‑search procedure results in the UE camping on a cell that is only 'acceptable' (not 'suitable') under TS 23.122 rules – e.g., no USIM/valid subscription context, no PLMN available for normal registration, or the found cell only supports limited service (such as emergency calls). In other words, the transition to LIMITED-SERVICE occurs when the lower layers indicate that a cell has been found and camped on, but that cell does not allow normal (suitable) service, so only limited service can be provided.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, subclause 5.2.2.3.2: 'LIMITED-SERVICE: This substate is entered when the UE has found a cell to camp on in accordance with the cell selection process specified in 3GPP TS 23.122, but normal service is not offered on that cell (i.e., only limited service, e.g. emergency calls, can be provided).'

results.question: In which scenarios after power on does the UE enter the NO-CELL-AVAILABLE substate following the initial PLMN-SEARCH state?
results.reference: The UE enters NO-CELL-AVAILABLE if: no cell can be selected; if in manual network selection mode and no cell of the selected PLMN has been found; or if the selected cell is a non-3GPP cell.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.2.1, Selection of the substate after power on
results.model_answer: After power-on, the UE first enters EMM-DEREGISTERED.PLMN-SEARCH while it performs PLMN selection (automatic or manual) to find a suitable PLMN/cell. The UE transitions from PLMN-SEARCH to EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE when the PLMN/cell selection procedure completes without finding any acceptable or suitable cell — i.e., the lower layers (AS) report to the NAS/EMM layer that no cell could be selected (no coverage, no acceptable PLMN found, or radio conditions prevent camping on any cell). This includes cases such as: (1) UE is powered on outside coverage of any PLMN, (2) UE performs a PLMN search and lower layers indicate 'no cell found' after scanning all frequencies/RATs, and (3) manual PLMN selection is attempted but no PLMN/cell satisfying selection criteria is found. Once a suitable cell is found later, the UE moves from NO-CELL-AVAILABLE back to PLMN-SEARCH or to NORMAL-SERVICE/LIMITED-SERVICE as appropriate.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Annex A (EMM sublayer states), sub-clause on EMM-DEREGISTERED substates: 'The UE enters the substate DEREGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE when the UE is unable to find a suitable or acceptable cell during PLMN and cell selection, i.e. when the lower layers indicate that no cell can be selected.'

results.question: What exception allows a UE to initiate an attach procedure even while timer T3346 is active?
results.reference: The UE may initiate an attach for emergency bearer services even if timer T3346 is running.
results.model_answer: A UE may initiate the attach procedure while timer T3346 (the mobility‑management back‑off timer) is still running only if the attach is being performed for emergency bearer services (i.e., the Attach Type IE indicates 'EMERGENCY'). In this case the UE is exempted from the T3346 restriction and is allowed to send the ATTACH REQUEST regardless of the timer state, because emergency services must not be blocked by congestion control back‑off timers.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §5.5.1.2.2 (Attach procedure initiation): 'The UE shall not start the attach procedure ... while timer T3346 is running, except when the attach procedure is initiated to establish an emergency PDN connection or for attach for emergency bearer services.'

results.question: Under what condition does the UE include the ESM message container IE?
results.reference: The UE includes the ESM message container IE when it wants to send an ESM message to the network.
results.model_answer: The ESM message container IE is not a mandatory part of every EMM message; the UE includes it only when it needs to piggyback (transfer) a specific ESM-layer message together with an EMM procedure message (e.g., TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST) because that ESM message cannot be sent as a stand-alone NAS message before the ongoing EMM signalling connection/procedure is completed. The most common and spec-cited case is during the tracking area updating procedure: if the UE has (or needs to establish) a PDN connection for emergency bearer services and this PDN connection must be moved between 3GPP and non-3GPP access, or the UE needs to request/re-establish such a PDN connection as part of the TAU procedure, the UE includes the ESM message container IE carrying the relevant ESM message (typically a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST) within the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST. More generally, the UE includes the ESM message container IE whenever it has ESM signalling (such as PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST, or BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION/MODIFICATION REQUEST) that must be delivered together with, or immediately following, an EMM procedure, rather than waiting for the completion of that EMM procedure to send it separately.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 §9.9.3.15 (ESM message container) and §5.5.3.2.2 – "The ESM message container IE is included if the UE needs to transfer an ESM message, e.g. a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message for emergency bearer services, during the tracking area updating procedure."

results.question: How can the network authorize a UAV flight when using USS, and during which procedures can this authorization be performed?
results.reference: The network can authorize a UAV flight using the UUAA-SM procedure, which can be performed either during the PDN connectivity procedure or during the bearer resource modification procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.4, Authorization of UAV flight
results.model_answer: In EPS, UAV flight authorization when a USS (UAS Service Supplier) is used is performed via the UUAA-MM (UAV Authentication and Authorization at Mobility Management level) procedure. The MME acts as a relay between the UE (UAV) and the USS/UAS-NF, forwarding CAA-level UAV identity and authentication/authorization payloads inside UAS NAS transport containers (piggybacked in UL/DL GENERIC NAS TRANSPORT messages carried within existing NAS signalling). The network can trigger or complete this USS-based authorization: (1) during the Attach procedure (initial UUAA-MM performed as part of, or immediately following, Attach when the UE indicates UAS capability/Aerial UE and requests C2 authorization), and (2) during the Tracking Area Update (TAU) procedure (re-authorization or periodic/triggered UUAA-MM when a valid authorization is not held or has expired). It can also be executed as a separate, stand-alone UUAA-MM exchange (using the generic UAS NAS transport procedure) after the UE is already registered, but the two mobility management procedures in which USS-based flight authorization is formally integrated are Attach and Tracking Area Update.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1 (Attach procedure) and clause 5.5.3 (Tracking area updating procedure), read together with the UUAA-MM procedure description (clause 5.5.1.2.3/5.5.3.2.3) specifying that UUAA-MM with the USS, via the UAS-NF, may be performed during the attach procedure or the tracking area update procedure.
